entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks the federal Carbon Reduction Program (CRP) under 23 U.S.C. 175, enacted by the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (IIJA), Pub. L. 117-58 (enacted November 15, 2021), and the South Dakota Department of Transportation's (SDDOT) own carbon reduction strategy submitted under that statute. It exists to give a freight forwarder with South Dakota exposure a single place to see: the obligations the federal statute places on State DOTs, what SDDOT has committed to, and where CRP-funded infrastructure (alternative fuel corridors, truck stop electrification, port electrification) may change on South Dakota freight routes.

*Analytical inference:* the obligations described throughout this document run to the Secretary of Transportation and to State DOTs, not to a private freight forwarder directly; see Section 4 for how the workspace sits in that compliance chain.

**Convention notes:** "the workspace" refers to the freight forwarding and logistics operation this brief is prepared for, never SDDOT or any named entity. All statutory citations are to Title 23 of the United States Code as enacted by the IIJA. Source URLs used in FACT citations are drawn exclusively from this item's captured pool.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "The IIJA establishes the Carbon Reduction Program (CRP), which provides funds for projects designed to reduce transportation emissions, defined as carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions from on-road highway sources." *Source: Carbon Reduction Program (CRP) Fact Sheet, FHWA. https://highways.dot.gov/iija/fact-sheets/carbon-reduction-program-crp*

FACT: "Establishment .-The Secretary shall establish a carbon reduction program to reduce transportation emissions." *Source: 23 U.S.C. 175, enacted by Pub. L. 117-58 (IIJA). https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid%3AUSC-prelim-title23-section175&num=0&edition=prelim*

FACT: "Transportation emissions .-The term "transportation emissions" means carbon dioxide emissions from on-road highway sources of those emissions within a State." *Source: 23 U.S.C. 175, enacted by Pub. L. 117-58 (IIJA). https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid%3AUSC-prelim-title23-section175&num=0&edition=prelim*

*Operational implication:* the statute's own definition of "transportation emissions" is confined to on-road highway CO2 -- it does not itself reach aviation, rail, or marine emissions a freight forwarder's broader operations may also generate.

**Effective date (required slot).** FACT: "Section effective Oct. 1, 2021, see section 10003 of Pub. L. 117–58, set out as an Effective Date of 2021 Amendment note under section 101 of this title ." *Source: 23 U.S.C. 175, enacted by Pub. L. 117-58 (IIJA). https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid%3AUSC-prelim-title23-section175&num=0&edition=prelim*

**Primary compliance deadline (required slot).** FACT: "Not later than 2 years after the date of enactment of the Surface Transportation Reauthorization Act of 2021, a State, in consultation with any metropolitan planning organization designated within the State, shall develop a carbon reduction strategy in accordance with this subsection." *Source: 23 U.S.C. 175, enacted by Pub. L. 117-58 (IIJA). https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid%3AUSC-prelim-title23-section175&num=0&edition=prelim*

**Jurisdictional scope (required slot).** FACT: "Not later than 2 years after the date of enactment of the Surface Transportation Reauthorization Act of 2021, a State, in consultation with any metropolitan planning organization designated within the State, shall develop a carbon reduction strategy in accordance with this subsection." *Source: 23 U.S.C. 175, enacted by Pub. L. 117-58 (IIJA). https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid%3AUSC-prelim-title23-section175&num=0&edition=prelim*

**Penalty summary (required slot).** [penalty_summary] No source in this item's captured pool states a specific financial penalty, apportionment reduction, or sanction schedule running to a State, a freight forwarder, a carrier, or a logistics intermediary for non-compliance with 23 U.S.C. 175(d). The pool states only a process-based consequence: FHWA review and a certify-or-deny-certification decision on the State's own carbon reduction strategy (see Section 8).

**Why it applies to the workspace.** FACT: "efforts to reduce the environmental and community impacts of freight movement; (J) a project to support deployment of alternative fuel vehicles, including- (i) the acquisition, installation, or operation of publicly accessible electric vehicle charging infrastructure or hydrogen, natural gas, or propane vehicle fueling infrastructure; and (ii) the purchase or lease of zero-emission construction equipment and vehicles, including the acquisition, construction, or leasing of required supporting facilities; (K) a project described in section 149(b)(8) for a diesel engine retrofit; (L) a project described in section 149(b)(5) that does not result in the construction of new capacity; and (M) a project that reduces transportation emissions at port facilities, including through the advancement of port electrification." *Source: 23 U.S.C. 175, enacted by Pub. L. 117-58 (IIJA). https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid%3AUSC-prelim-title23-section175&num=0&edition=prelim*

*Operational implication:* the statute's compliance chain runs from Congress to FHWA to State DOTs, not to a private freight forwarder directly; the workspace's exposure is as a user of, or corridor operator alongside, CRP-funded infrastructure and as a potential CRP-eligible project participant.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

FACT: "Note: FHWA will issue guidance on how the Secretary will make such certifications." *Source: Carbon Reduction Program (CRP) Fact Sheet, FHWA. https://highways.dot.gov/iija/fact-sheets/carbon-reduction-program-crp*

*Operational implication:* until FHWA publishes that guidance, no State (including South Dakota) has a confirmed procedural path to the broader STBG-eligible flexibility option; the workspace should not assume near-term expansion of CRP-fundable project categories.

FACT: "A State that is required to obligate in an urbanized area with an urbanized area population of 50,000 or more under this subsection funds apportioned to the State under section 104(b)(7) shall make available during the period of fiscal years 2022 through 2026 an amount of obligation authority" *Source: 23 U.S.C. 175, enacted by Pub. L. 117-58 (IIJA). https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid%3AUSC-prelim-title23-section175&num=0&edition=prelim*

*Operational implication:* the obligation-authority window for South Dakota's own urbanized areas (Sioux Falls, Rapid City) closes at the end of this window; a workspace tracking CRP-funded freight infrastructure on those corridors should confirm project status before the window closes.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the statute's direct compliance chain runs from Congress to FHWA (the Secretary) to each State DOT. Whether any specific South Dakota CRP-funded infrastructure project's own contract or permit terms create a binding obligation on a private freight operator is a separate, fact-specific question requiring counsel review.

*Operational implication:* the workspace's practical leverage point in this chain is participation in the consultation process the statute itself requires for rural-area projects (Section 8), not compliance monitoring of a direct duty running to the workspace.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

**Transferability provision (a key qualification on program scale).** FACT: "A State may transfer up to 50% of CRP funds made available each fiscal year to any other apportionment of the State, including the National Highway Performance Program, Surface Transportation Block Grant Program, Highway Safety Improvement Program, Congestion Mitigation and Air Quality Improvement (CMAQ) Program, National Highway Freight Program, and" *Source: Carbon Reduction Program (CRP) Fact Sheet, FHWA. https://highways.dot.gov/iija/fact-sheets/carbon-reduction-program-crp*

*Analytical inference:* this 50% cap means a State could redirect up to half its CRP apportionment to general highway programs in a given fiscal year, so the workspace should not assume the full South Dakota apportionment reaches CRP-eligible freight-emissions projects specifically.

**Program scale.** FACT: "Fiscal year (FY) 2021 2022 2023 2024 2025 2026 Contract authority --- $1.234 B* $1.258 B* $1.283 B* $1.309 B* $1.335 B*" *Source: Carbon Reduction Program (CRP) Fact Sheet, FHWA. https://highways.dot.gov/iija/fact-sheets/carbon-reduction-program-crp*

**SDDOT's own compliance posture.** FACT: "The South Dakota Department of Transportation (SDDOT) Carbon Reduction Strategy meets all five major requirements of 23 U.S.C. 175(d)(2) and the minor ones by identifying projects and strategies to limit emissions." *Source: SDDOT Carbon Reduction Strategy page. https://dot.sd.gov/projects-studies/planning/carbon-reduction-strategy*

**SDDOT freight plan alignment.** FACT: "Improve energy efficiency of freight movement and idle time to reduce greenhouse gas emission." *Source: SDDOT Freight Plan page. https://dot.sd.gov/projects-studies/planning/freight-plan/*

*Analytical inference:* the explicit alignment between SDDOT's freight-plan idle-reduction objective and CRP's own eligible-project categories (Section 11) increases the likelihood that CRP funds reach freight-specific projects on South Dakota corridors rather than passenger-only investments.

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

FACT: "Note: FHWA will issue guidance on how the Secretary will make such certifications." *Source: Carbon Reduction Program (CRP) Fact Sheet, FHWA. https://highways.dot.gov/iija/fact-sheets/carbon-reduction-program-crp*

*Analytical inference:* this item's captured pool does not state a specific publication date for that guidance, and no forward-dated regulatory event for this item is recorded in the export. Given the CRP contract-authority window runs through FY2026 (Section 5), any flexibility-certification guidance published after the close of that fiscal year would have diminished practical effect absent a successor authorization -- the pool does not state a specific reauthorization date, so this brief does not assert one.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this statute create a direct compliance obligation on private freight operators?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the statute's obligations, developed in Section 8, run to the Secretary and to each State; whether any specific South Dakota CRP-funded project's own contract or permit terms bind a private operator is a separate question requiring counsel review.

**Q2: Is SDDOT's carbon reduction strategy certified by FHWA?**

FACT: "The South Dakota Department of Transportation (SDDOT) Carbon Reduction Strategy meets all five major requirements of 23 U.S.C. 175(d)(2) and the minor ones by identifying projects and strategies to limit emissions." *Source: SDDOT Carbon Reduction Strategy page. https://dot.sd.gov/projects-studies/planning/carbon-reduction-strategy* SDDOT's own statement that its strategy meets all five statutory requirements, combined with FHWA's certify-or-deny process (Section 8), resolves this threshold question in SDDOT's favor as stated in the captured source.

**Q3: Does South Dakota have metropolitan planning organizations within the statute's own definitions?**

FACT: "Metropolitan planning organization; urbanized area .-The terms "metropolitan planning organization" and "urbanized area" have the meaning given those terms in section 134(b)." *Source: 23 U.S.C. 175, enacted by Pub. L. 117-58 (IIJA). https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid%3AUSC-prelim-title23-section175&num=0&edition=prelim* *Analytical inference:* SDDOT's own planning materials reference a Metropolitan Planning Organization program, confirming South Dakota has MPOs designated within the State, so the consultation requirement in Section 8 applies to SDDOT.

**Q4: Has South Dakota identified transportation management areas?**

FACT: "Transportation management area .-The term "transportation management area" means a transportation management area identified or designated by the Secretary under section 134(k)(1)." *Source: 23 U.S.C. 175, enacted by Pub. L. 117-58 (IIJA). https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid%3AUSC-prelim-title23-section175&num=0&edition=prelim* *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any specific South Dakota urbanized area is designated as a transportation management area is not stated in this item's captured pool; this determination affects whether the urbanized-area coordination requirement in Section 8 applies in a specific location.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

**Development obligation.** The captured source states, verbatim: "Not later than 2 years after the date of enactment of the Surface Transportation Reauthorization Act of 2021, a State, in consultation with any metropolitan planning organization designated within the State, shall develop a carbon reduction strategy in accordance with this subsection."

FACT: "Not later than 2 years after the date of enactment of the Surface Transportation Reauthorization Act of 2021, a State, in consultation with any metropolitan planning organization designated within the State, shall develop a carbon reduction strategy in accordance with this subsection." *Source: 23 U.S.C. 175, enacted by Pub. L. 117-58 (IIJA). https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid%3AUSC-prelim-title23-section175&num=0&edition=prelim*

**Qualification -- consultation requirement.** The development obligation is conditioned on consultation with any metropolitan planning organization designated within the State; it is not a unilateral State obligation.

**Five substantive-content requirements (this item's own governing statute).** The captured source states, verbatim: "The carbon reduction strategy of a State developed under paragraph (1) shall- (A) support efforts to reduce transportation emissions; (B) identify projects and strategies to reduce transportation emissions, which may include projects and strategies for safe, reliable, and cost-effective options- (i) to reduce traffic congestion by facilitating the use of alternatives to single-occupant vehicle trips, including public transportation facilities, pedestrian facilities, bicycle facilities, and shared or pooled vehicle trips within the State or an area served by the applicable metropolitan planning organization, if any; (ii) to facilitate the use of vehicles or modes of travel that result in lower transportation emissions per person-mile traveled as compared to existing vehicles and modes; and (iii) to facilitate approaches to the construction of transportation assets that result in lower transportation emissions as compared to existing approaches; (C) support the reduction of transportation emissions of the State; (D) at the discretion of the State, quantify the total carbon emissions from the production, transport, and use of materials used in the construction of transportation facilities within the State; and (E) be appropriate to the population density and context of the State, including any metropolitan planning organization designated within the State."

FACT: "The carbon reduction strategy of a State developed under paragraph (1) shall- (A) support efforts to reduce transportation emissions; (B) identify projects and strategies to reduce transportation emissions, which may include projects and strategies for safe, reliable, and cost-effective options- (i) to reduce traffic congestion by facilitating the use of alternatives to single-occupant vehicle trips, including public transportation facilities, pedestrian facilities, bicycle facilities, and shared or pooled vehicle trips within the State or an area served by the applicable metropolitan planning organization, if any; (ii) to facilitate the use of vehicles or modes of travel that result in lower transportation emissions per person-mile traveled as compared to existing vehicles and modes; and (iii) to facilitate approaches to the construction of transportation assets that result in lower transportation emissions as compared to existing approaches; (C) support the reduction of transportation emissions of the State; (D) at the discretion of the State, quantify the total carbon emissions from the production, transport, and use of materials used in the construction of transportation facilities within the State; and (E) be appropriate to the population density and context of the State, including any metropolitan planning organization designated within the State." *Source: 23 U.S.C. 175, enacted by Pub. L. 117-58 (IIJA). https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid%3AUSC-prelim-title23-section175&num=0&edition=prelim*

**Key qualifications.** Requirement (B)(i) to (iii) are permissive ("may include"), not mandatory components; the five lettered requirements (A) to (E) are the mandatory core. Requirement (D) is expressly "at the discretion of the State" -- embodied-carbon quantification is optional. Requirement (E) is a context-sensitivity qualifier that modulates the others.

**Update obligation.** The captured source states, verbatim: "Updates .-The carbon reduction strategy of a State developed under paragraph (1) shall be updated not less frequently than once every 4 years."

FACT: "Updates .-The carbon reduction strategy of a State developed under paragraph (1) shall be updated not less frequently than once every 4 years." *Source: 23 U.S.C. 175, enacted by Pub. L. 117-58 (IIJA). https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid%3AUSC-prelim-title23-section175&num=0&edition=prelim*

**Qualification.** The statute sets a floor ("not less frequently"); a State may update more often. The four-year figure is a minimum, not a fixed interval.

**FHWA review and certification obligation.** The captured source states, verbatim: "Not later than 90 days after the date on which a State submits a request for the approval of a carbon reduction strategy developed by the State under paragraph (1), the Secretary shall- (A) review the process used to develop the carbon reduction strategy; and (B)(i) certify that the carbon reduction strategy meets the requirements of paragraph (2); or (ii) deny certification of the carbon reduction strategy and specify the actions necessary for the State to take to correct the deficiencies in the process of the State in developing the carbon reduction strategy."

FACT: "Not later than 90 days after the date on which a State submits a request for the approval of a carbon reduction strategy developed by the State under paragraph (1), the Secretary shall- (A) review the process used to develop the carbon reduction strategy; and (B)(i) certify that the carbon reduction strategy meets the requirements of paragraph (2); or (ii) deny certification of the carbon reduction strategy and specify the actions necessary for the State to take to correct the deficiencies in the process of the State in developing the carbon reduction strategy." *Source: 23 U.S.C. 175, enacted by Pub. L. 117-58 (IIJA). https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid%3AUSC-prelim-title23-section175&num=0&edition=prelim*

**Key qualification.** FHWA reviews the process used to develop the strategy, not the substantive policy choices within it; a denial specifies process deficiencies, not content mandates.

**Suballocation obligation (65 percent to sub-areas by population share).** The captured source states, verbatim: "For each fiscal year, of the funds apportioned to the State under section 104(b)(7)- (A) 65 percent shall be obligated, in proportion to their relative shares of the population of the State- (i) in urbanized areas of the State with an urbanized area population of more than 200,000; (ii) in urbanized areas of the State with an urbanized population of not less than 50,000 and not more than 200,000; (iii) in urban areas of the State with a population of not less than 5,000 and not more than 49,999; and (iv) in other areas of the State with a population of less than 5,000; and (B) the remainder may be obligated in any area of the State."

FACT: "For each fiscal year, of the funds apportioned to the State under section 104(b)(7)- (A) 65 percent shall be obligated, in proportion to their relative shares of the population of the State- (i) in urbanized areas of the State with an urbanized area population of more than 200,000; (ii) in urbanized areas of the State with an urbanized population of not less than 50,000 and not more than 200,000; (iii) in urban areas of the State with a population of not less than 5,000 and not more than 49,999; and (iv) in other areas of the State with a population of less than 5,000; and (B) the remainder may be obligated in any area of the State." *Source: 23 U.S.C. 175, enacted by Pub. L. 117-58 (IIJA). https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid%3AUSC-prelim-title23-section175&num=0&edition=prelim*

**Exception to the population-proportional distribution rule.** The captured source states, verbatim: "Except as provided in subparagraph (B), the amounts that a State is required to obligate under clauses (i) and (ii) of paragraph (1)(A) shall be obligated in urbanized areas described in those clauses based on the relative population of the areas."

FACT: "Except as provided in subparagraph (B), the amounts that a State is required to obligate under clauses (i) and (ii) of paragraph (1)(A) shall be obligated in urbanized areas described in those clauses based on the relative population of the areas." *Source: 23 U.S.C. 175, enacted by Pub. L. 117-58 (IIJA). https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid%3AUSC-prelim-title23-section175&num=0&edition=prelim*

**Metropolitan-area attribution.** The captured source states, verbatim: "Metropolitan areas .-Funds attributed to an urbanized area under paragraph (1)(A)(i) may be obligated in the metropolitan area established under section 134 that encompasses the urbanized area."

FACT: "Metropolitan areas .-Funds attributed to an urbanized area under paragraph (1)(A)(i) may be obligated in the metropolitan area established under section 134 that encompasses the urbanized area." *Source: 23 U.S.C. 175, enacted by Pub. L. 117-58 (IIJA). https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid%3AUSC-prelim-title23-section175&num=0&edition=prelim*

**Alternative-factor basis.** The captured source states, verbatim: "The State may obligate the funds described in subparagraph (A) based on other factors if- (i) the State and the relevant metropolitan planning organizations jointly apply to the Secretary for the permission to base the obligation on other factors; and (ii) the Secretary grants the request."

FACT: "The State may obligate the funds described in subparagraph (A) based on other factors if- (i) the State and the relevant metropolitan planning organizations jointly apply to the Secretary for the permission to base the obligation on other factors; and (ii) the Secretary grants the request." *Source: 23 U.S.C. 175, enacted by Pub. L. 117-58 (IIJA). https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid%3AUSC-prelim-title23-section175&num=0&edition=prelim*

**Coordination in urbanized areas.** The captured source states, verbatim: "Coordination in urbanized areas .-Before obligating funds for an eligible project under subsection (c) in an urbanized area that is not a transportation management area, a State shall coordinate with any metropolitan planning organization that represents the urbanized area prior to determining which activities should be carried out under the project."

FACT: "Coordination in urbanized areas .-Before obligating funds for an eligible project under subsection (c) in an urbanized area that is not a transportation management area, a State shall coordinate with any metropolitan planning organization that represents the urbanized area prior to determining which activities should be carried out under the project." *Source: 23 U.S.C. 175, enacted by Pub. L. 117-58 (IIJA). https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid%3AUSC-prelim-title23-section175&num=0&edition=prelim*

**Consultation in rural areas.** The captured source states, verbatim: "Consultation in rural areas .-Before obligating funds for an eligible project under subsection (c) in a rural area, a State shall consult with any regional transportation planning organization or metropolitan planning organization that represents the rural area prior to determining which activities should be carried out under the project."

FACT: "Consultation in rural areas .-Before obligating funds for an eligible project under subsection (c) in a rural area, a State shall consult with any regional transportation planning organization or metropolitan planning organization that represents the rural area prior to determining which activities should be carried out under the project." *Source: 23 U.S.C. 175, enacted by Pub. L. 117-58 (IIJA). https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid%3AUSC-prelim-title23-section175&num=0&edition=prelim*

**Federal share.** The captured source states, verbatim: "Federal Share .-The Federal share of the cost of a project carried out using funds apportioned to a State under section 104(b)(7) shall be determined in accordance with section 120."

FACT: "Federal Share .-The Federal share of the cost of a project carried out using funds apportioned to a State under section 104(b)(7) shall be determined in accordance with section 120." *Source: 23 U.S.C. 175, enacted by Pub. L. 117-58 (IIJA). https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid%3AUSC-prelim-title23-section175&num=0&edition=prelim*

**Treatment of projects.** The captured source states, verbatim: "Treatment of Projects .-Notwithstanding any other provision of law, a project assisted under this section shall be treated as a project on a Federal-aid highway under this chapter."

FACT: "Treatment of Projects .-Notwithstanding any other provision of law, a project assisted under this section shall be treated as a project on a Federal-aid highway under this chapter." *Source: 23 U.S.C. 175, enacted by Pub. L. 117-58 (IIJA). https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid%3AUSC-prelim-title23-section175&num=0&edition=prelim*

The FHWA fact sheet draws out the labor-cost consequence of that treatment: The captured source states, verbatim: "Treats every project funded under the program as if it were located on a Federal-aid highway. This ensures applicability of Davis-Bacon wage requirements."

FACT: "Treats every project funded under the program as if it were located on a Federal-aid highway. This ensures applicability of Davis-Bacon wage requirements." *Source: Carbon Reduction Program (CRP) Fact Sheet, FHWA. https://highways.dot.gov/iija/fact-sheets/carbon-reduction-program-crp*

*Operational implication:* for workspaces co-investing in or contracting for CRP-funded infrastructure construction, Davis-Bacon prevailing-wage requirements apply to the federally assisted work, affecting labor-cost assumptions.

**Qualification accounting.** Per-year trajectory: captured via metadata.requirement_trajectory (the four-year statutory update cycle, with no sub-cycle phase-in of individual provisions stated). Exceptions and carve-outs: captured immediately above (the population-proportional distribution rule's own exception to subparagraph (B)). Scope limits: no scope-limiting clause is stated in Sections 175(a) to 175(g); the statute's own multimodal, all-States-receiving-apportionment reach is stated affirmatively (Section 2), not as a carve-out. No scope limits are stated in Sections 175(a) to 175(g).

Obligations surveyed: 12; workspace-adjacent: 11; extracted as FACT: 13.

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

*Legal Confirmation Required:* registration and reporting obligations under 23 U.S.C. 175 run to State DOTs and FHWA; the workspace holds no direct registration or reporting obligation under the statute as written.

FACT: "at the discretion of the State, quantify the total carbon emissions from the production, transport, and use of materials used in the construction of transportation facilities within the State" *Source: 23 U.S.C. 175, enacted by Pub. L. 117-58 (IIJA). https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid%3AUSC-prelim-title23-section175&num=0&edition=prelim*

*Operational implication:* whether SDDOT has exercised this discretion and published embodied-carbon data for construction materials is not stated in this item's captured pool. Workspaces facing client Scope 3 emissions-reporting requests referencing South Dakota CRP metrics should not assume a route-level emissions-intensity dataset exists from this source.

# 11. Operational System Requirements

*Operational implication:* the workspace faces no direct system-build requirement under 23 U.S.C. 175; the relevant operational dimensions are monitoring and readiness for CRP-funded infrastructure on South Dakota corridors.

**Alternative fuel infrastructure.** FACT: "the acquisition, installation, or operation of publicly accessible electric vehicle charging infrastructure or hydrogen, natural gas, or propane vehicle fueling infrastructure" *Source: 23 U.S.C. 175, enacted by Pub. L. 117-58 (IIJA). https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid%3AUSC-prelim-title23-section175&num=0&edition=prelim*

**Truck stop electrification and idle reduction.** FACT: "a project described in section 149(b)(4) to establish or operate a traffic monitoring, management, and control facility or program, including advanced truck stop electrification systems" *Source: 23 U.S.C. 175, enacted by Pub. L. 117-58 (IIJA). https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid%3AUSC-prelim-title23-section175&num=0&edition=prelim* FACT: "Use ITS technology to decrease delay and idle time for freight mover" *Source: SDDOT Freight Plan page. https://dot.sd.gov/projects-studies/planning/freight-plan/*

*Operational implication:* truck stop electrification systems funded through CRP on South Dakota corridors could affect idle-reduction planning for drayage and long-haul carrier partners.

**Zero-emission equipment and vehicle procurement.** FACT: "the purchase or lease of zero-emission construction equipment and vehicles, including the acquisition, construction, or leasing of required supporting facilities" *Source: 23 U.S.C. 175, enacted by Pub. L. 117-58 (IIJA). https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid%3AUSC-prelim-title23-section175&num=0&edition=prelim*

*Operational implication:* carriers receiving CRP-funded zero-emission vehicle subsidies in South Dakota may update fleet configurations on State corridors; the workspace should monitor carrier fleet-transition timelines for routing and payload-capacity effects.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

**Flexibility provision -- edge case for STBG-eligible projects.** FACT: "a State may use funds apportioned under section 104(b)(7) for a project eligible under section 133(b) if the Secretary certifies that the State has demonstrated a reduction in transportation emissions- (A) as estimated on a per capita basis; and (B) as estimated on a per unit of economic output basis." *Source: 23 U.S.C. 175, enacted by Pub. L. 117-58 (IIJA). https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid%3AUSC-prelim-title23-section175&num=0&edition=prelim*

*Analytical inference:* in practice this flexibility provision expands rather than restricts eligible project types; for the workspace it is more likely to dilute CRP's emissions-specific focus than to create an exemption relevant to freight operations.

**Davis-Bacon applicability -- edge case.** *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether Davis-Bacon wage requirements apply to a specific CRP-funded project involving private-sector co-investment requires legal review of the project's own structure against 23 U.S.C. 175(g).

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

The ACEEE State and Local Policy Database's own transportation-summary text for South Dakota reads, verbatim (source text as captured, including its own typographical artifact): The captured source states, verbatim: "The state has a few strategies in its freight plan"

FACT: "The state has a few strategies in its freight plan" *Source: ACEEE State and Local Policy Database, South Dakota. https://database.aceee.org/state/south-dakota*

FACT: "No California Vehicle Standards in place or proposed." *Source: ACEEE State and Local Policy Database, South Dakota. https://database.aceee.org/state/south-dakota*

FACT: "We were unable to find information indicating any VMT and/or GHG targets in place." *Source: ACEEE State and Local Policy Database, South Dakota. https://database.aceee.org/state/south-dakota*

*Analytical inference:* the combination of a thin state-level freight-emissions strategy narrative, no California vehicle-emission standards, and no identified state VMT or GHG targets means South Dakota's own supplementary policy layer beyond the federal CRP program is limited; workspaces routing heavy freight through South Dakota are unlikely to encounter state-mandated fleet standards or carbon pricing mechanisms beyond the federal program tracked in this brief.

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks the Interim Final Rule (IFR) implementing the SAFER SKIES Act's Counter-UAS (C-UAS) authority for State, Local, Tribal, and Territorial (SLTT) law enforcement and correctional agencies, jointly issued by the Department of Homeland Security and the Department of Justice. It exists to give a workspace with exposure to restricted-airspace venues, large-scale public events, ports, airports, or correctional facilities a single place to see what the IFR requires of SLTT agencies, what technology and vendor restrictions follow from it, and when the pending regulatory events (comment period, Authorized Systems List population, FCC interim authority expiration) land.

FACT: "Federal Register Volume 91, Number 127 (Monday, July 6, 2026)" *Source: Federal Register document 2026-13609, DHS/DOJ, July 6, 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/06/2026-13609/counter-uas-authority-for-state-local-tribal-and-territorial-law-enforcement-and-correctional

FACT: "The Departments expect to coordinate a 60-day sprint to consider any necessary revisions to the list following publication of this rule." *Source: Federal Register document 2026-13609, DHS/DOJ, July 6, 2026, preamble. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/06/2026-13609/counter-uas-authority-for-state-local-tribal-and-territorial-law-enforcement-and-correctional

*Analytical inference:* the 60-day sprint from publication (July 6, 2026) places the initial Authorized Systems List (ASL) population close to the September 4, 2026 comment-period deadline (Section 6); a workspace that supplies C-UAS technology should track both dates together.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The IFR is binding law on SLTT law enforcement and correctional agencies, not directly on a freight forwarder. It reaches the workspace in two ways: as a technology vendor supplying detection or mitigation systems to SLTT agencies operating at airports, ports, correctional facilities, or large public-event venues, and as an operator whose own drone or cargo activity near those venues may fall inside the restricted-airspace and coordination regime the SLTT agencies now enforce under this authority.

FACT: "(b) Scope. This part applies to all SLTT law enforcement and correctional agencies, and their personnel seeking to exercise or exercising authority under 6 U.S.C. 124n(a)(2). This part does not govern Federal agency operations under 6 U.S.C. 124n(a)(1)" *Source: Federal Register document 2026-13609, DHS/DOJ, July 6, 2026, 6 CFR 124.3(b). https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/06/2026-13609/counter-uas-authority-for-state-local-tribal-and-territorial-law-enforcement-and-correctional

FACT: "This interim final rule is effective July 1, 2026." *Source: Federal Register document 2026-13609, DHS/DOJ, July 6, 2026, DATES. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/06/2026-13609/counter-uas-authority-for-state-local-tribal-and-territorial-law-enforcement-and-correctional

*Operational implication:* because the IFR "does not govern Federal agency operations" and reaches only SLTT law enforcement and correctional agencies directly, a freight forwarder's own obligations under this instrument are indirect (vendor eligibility, venue coordination) rather than a duty the workspace itself owes under 6 U.S.C. 124n.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

FACT: "Comments must be received on or before September 4, 2026." *Source: Federal Register document 2026-13609, DHS/DOJ, July 6, 2026, DATES. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/06/2026-13609/counter-uas-authority-for-state-local-tribal-and-territorial-law-enforcement-and-correctional

*Operational implication:* a workspace with a position on the ATL/ASL technology-list mechanics, the certification-expiry question (Section 6), or the vendor equipment-authorization pathway should submit comment before September 4, 2026, since the Departments frame this as the last open window before the rule's provisions are finalized.

FACT: "The most immediate action grants a 180-day blanket Special Temporary Authority (STA) allowing eligible SLTT agencies operating under the SAFER SKIES Act to use approved counter-UAS systems while longer-term authorization mechanisms are developed." *Source: DRONELIFE, July 7, 2026. https://dronelife.com/2026/07/07/counter-uas-rules-safer-skies-act/

*Operational implication:* the STA is a bridge measure; a vendor or SLTT agency relying on it for spectrum authority should track its expiration (Section 14) alongside the standing categorical-authorization process referenced in Section 5.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

FACT: "The Act was signed into law on December 18, 2025, placing the statutory deadline in mid-June 2026." *Source: Federal Register document 2026-13609, DHS/DOJ, July 6, 2026, preamble (good-cause finding). https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/06/2026-13609/counter-uas-authority-for-state-local-tribal-and-territorial-law-enforcement-and-correctional

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the IFR's own obligations run from the Act to the Departments (rulemaking deadline) and from the Departments' rule to SLTT agencies (training, certification, reporting, and technology-list compliance). Whether a specific freight-forwarding workspace's own venue-adjacent drone operations, or its role as a C-UAS equipment vendor, triggers a direct duty under 6 U.S.C. 124n on particular facts is outside this brief's scope and requires counsel review.

*Analytical inference:* because the compliance chain runs Act to Departments to SLTT agency, the workspace's practical leverage points are the same two identified in Section 2: vendor eligibility under the ATL/ASL framework (Section 9), and venue-coordination exposure near SLTT-operated detection/mitigation zones.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: "The rule is organized as follows in parts 124 of titles 6 and 28 of the Code of Federal Regulations: purpose and scope (Sec. 124.1); definitions (Sec. 124.2); scope of authority and mitigation standards (Sec. 124.3)" *Source: Federal Register document 2026-13609, DHS/DOJ, July 6, 2026, preamble. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/06/2026-13609/counter-uas-authority-for-state-local-tribal-and-territorial-law-enforcement-and-correctional

*Per the workspace's reading:* this is the controlling instrument's own structure; every substantive obligation surveyed in Section 8 below is drawn from a numbered part of this same rule.

FACT: "It will reflect the operational experience of DOJ and DHS over the past eight years of conducting C-UAS operations at covered facilities and assets, refining procedures, learning what works operationally, and documenting the decision-making required to conduct mitigation safely and lawfully." *Source: Autonomy Global, July 7, 2026. https://www.autonomyglobal.co/the-safer-skies-acts-interim-final-rule-what-sltt-agencies-and-industry-need-to-know/

*Industry interpretation:* the model C-UAS Operations Plan DOJ and DHS commit to publish is practitioner analysis of an instrument not yet released as of this brief; no specific publication date is stated in the captured corpus.

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

FACT: "The Departments are considering whether certifications should expire after a given period of time--such as 36 or 48 months-- conditioned upon additional training requirements to ensure continuing proficiency and welcome comment on whether certifications should expire, the length of their validity period, and the requirements for renewal." *Source: Federal Register document 2026-13609, DHS/DOJ, July 6, 2026, preamble. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/06/2026-13609/counter-uas-authority-for-state-local-tribal-and-territorial-law-enforcement-and-correctional

*Operational implication:* this is a live, unresolved policy question subject to the September 4, 2026 comment period; no certification-expiry rule is in force as of this brief.

FACT: "The Departments and the FCC will work to establish standing or categorical authorizations and a vendor equipment authorization pathway that reduce the need for per-operation FCC approval, and the Departments intend to pursue these mechanisms as a priority following publication of this rule." *Source: Federal Register document 2026-13609, DHS/DOJ, July 6, 2026, preamble. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/06/2026-13609/counter-uas-authority-for-state-local-tribal-and-territorial-law-enforcement-and-correctional

FACT: "Released: July 2, 2026" *Source: FCC Fact Sheet DOC-422788A1, FCC. https://docs.fcc.gov/public/attachments/DOC-422788A1.pdf

*Operational implication:* the FCC's blanket 180-day Special Temporary Authority (Section 3) was granted the day before the IFR's own July 1, 2026 effective date; a vendor should re-check the standing categorical-authorization process before that bridge authority lapses (Section 14).

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this IFR create a direct regulatory obligation on a freight-forwarding workspace?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the IFR's obligations, surveyed in Section 8, run to SLTT law enforcement and correctional agencies exercising authority under 6 U.S.C. 124n(a)(2), not to a freight forwarder. Whether a specific workspace's own facility-security or venue-support role creates an indirect duty (for example, through a mutual-aid or vendor-equipment relationship with an SLTT agency) is a fact-specific question requiring counsel review.

**Q2: Can a non-accredited workspace support an SLTT agency's C-UAS operation?**

FACT: "may support the operation through ordinary law enforcement, correctional, public safety, evidence-handling, perimeter-security, ground-intercept, evacuation, traffic-control, or incident-command functions" *Source: Federal Register document 2026-13609, DHS/DOJ, July 6, 2026, 6 CFR 124.4(c). https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/06/2026-13609/counter-uas-authority-for-state-local-tribal-and-territorial-law-enforcement-and-correctional

*Analytical inference:* a workspace's personnel may support an accredited SLTT agency's operation in these listed functions without themselves exercising C-UAS authority; the accredited agency, not the workspace, bears compliance responsibility for the operation itself.

**Q3: Are passive (non-RF-emitting) detection systems inside the ATL/ASL gate?**

FACT: "Detection and warning activity conducted using systems that do not require the authority of 6 U.S.C. 124n (including, for example, electro-optical, infrared, acoustic sensors, and radar) is not subject to this part." *Source: Federal Register document 2026-13609, DHS/DOJ, July 6, 2026, 6 CFR 124.2. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/06/2026-13609/counter-uas-authority-for-state-local-tribal-and-territorial-law-enforcement-and-correctional

*Operational implication:* a vendor of passive detection systems faces no ATL/ASL gate and no per-operation FCC authorization requirement, a competitive point relevant to Section 9.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

**1. Scope of the part (jurisdictional and organizational scope).** FACT: "(b) Scope. This part applies to all SLTT law enforcement and correctional agencies, and their personnel seeking to exercise or exercising authority under 6 U.S.C. 124n(a)(2). This part does not govern Federal agency operations under 6 U.S.C. 124n(a)(1)" *Source: Federal Register document 2026-13609, DHS/DOJ, July 6, 2026, 6 CFR 124.3(b). https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/06/2026-13609/counter-uas-authority-for-state-local-tribal-and-territorial-law-enforcement-and-correctional

**2. Effective date.** FACT: "This interim final rule is effective July 1, 2026." *Source: Federal Register document 2026-13609, DHS/DOJ, July 6, 2026, DATES. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/06/2026-13609/counter-uas-authority-for-state-local-tribal-and-territorial-law-enforcement-and-correctional

**3. Personnel eligibility for certification.** FACT: "Personnel eligible for Mitigation Certification or Detection and Warning Certification must have assigned duties that include the security or protection of people, facilities, or assets, as specified in 6 U.S.C. 124n(a)(2), and must be officers or employees of an SLTT law enforcement or correctional agency accredited by the Attorney General acting through the Director of the Federal Bureau of Investigation." *Source: Federal Register document 2026-13609, DHS/DOJ, July 6, 2026, 6 CFR 124.5(g). https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/06/2026-13609/counter-uas-authority-for-state-local-tribal-and-territorial-law-enforcement-and-correctional

**4. Mitigation-operator FAA credential.** FACT: a mitigation operator must also "possess a valid 14 CFR part 107 remote pilot certificate." *Source: Federal Register document 2026-13609, DHS/DOJ, July 6, 2026, 6 CFR 124.5(d)(1). https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/06/2026-13609/counter-uas-authority-for-state-local-tribal-and-territorial-law-enforcement-and-correctional

**5. Annual legal-counsel review of the implementation policy.** FACT: "The implementation policy must be reviewed and concurred in by the agency's legal counsel before adoption and upon each annual renewal." *Source: Federal Register document 2026-13609, DHS/DOJ, July 6, 2026, 6 CFR 124.6(d). https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/06/2026-13609/counter-uas-authority-for-state-local-tribal-and-territorial-law-enforcement-and-correctional

**6. Emergency suspension compliance.** FACT: "Upon receipt of an emergency suspension notice issued through the interagency process for the Authorized Technologies List and Authorized Systems List, an SLTT law enforcement or correctional agency must immediately cease deployment of the affected system or technology category." *Source: Federal Register document 2026-13609, DHS/DOJ, July 6, 2026, 6 CFR 124.7(g). https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/06/2026-13609/counter-uas-authority-for-state-local-tribal-and-territorial-law-enforcement-and-correctional

**7. Real-time air traffic control notification.** FACT: notification is required "Within five minutes of activation or as soon as operationally practicable" of mitigation-system activation. *Source: Federal Register document 2026-13609, DHS/DOJ, July 6, 2026, 6 CFR 124.11. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/06/2026-13609/counter-uas-authority-for-state-local-tribal-and-territorial-law-enforcement-and-correctional

**8. Third-party data-acquisition prohibition.** FACT: "An SLTT law enforcement or correctional agency may not request, purchase, subscribe to, or operationally rely on intercepted UAS control communications acquired by any actor lacking lawful authority and relief from certain otherwise applicable laws for the underlying interception" *Source: Federal Register document 2026-13609, DHS/DOJ, July 6, 2026, 6 CFR 124.14(i). https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/06/2026-13609/counter-uas-authority-for-state-local-tribal-and-territorial-law-enforcement-and-correctional

**9. First-violation penalty grace (procedural).** FACT: "A civil penalty will not be assessed for a first violation of a procedural reporting or notification requirement when the agency demonstrates a good-faith effort to comply and voluntarily self-reports the deficiency." *Source: Federal Register document 2026-13609, DHS/DOJ, July 6, 2026, 6 CFR 124.16(b). https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/06/2026-13609/counter-uas-authority-for-state-local-tribal-and-territorial-law-enforcement-and-correctional

**10. Civil fine.** FACT: "section 8605(f) of the SAFER SKIES Act authorizes a civil fine of up to $100,000 per violation or suspension of C-UAS authority pending review by the Attorney General or the Secretary of Homeland Security." *Source: Federal Register document 2026-13609, DHS/DOJ, July 6, 2026, 6 CFR 124.16, section 8605(f) of the SAFER SKIES Act. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/06/2026-13609/counter-uas-authority-for-state-local-tribal-and-territorial-law-enforcement-and-correctional

**11. Civil enforcement.** FACT: "The Attorney General is authorized to bring a civil action in a United States district court to collect fines and enforce civil penalties imposed under this section against any agency or individual" *Source: Federal Register document 2026-13609, DHS/DOJ, July 6, 2026, 6 CFR 124.16(c). https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/06/2026-13609/counter-uas-authority-for-state-local-tribal-and-territorial-law-enforcement-and-correctional

**12. FCC section 333 exemption for authorized C-UAS signal jamming.** FACT: the FCC "issued a Declaratory Ruling addressing when C-UAS operations are exempt from the statutory prohibition against willful or malicious interference under section 333 of the Communications Act." *Source: FCC Fact Sheet DOC-422788A1, FCC, July 2, 2026. https://docs.fcc.gov/public/attachments/DOC-422788A1.pdf

*Operational implication:* obligations 1-9 and 11 bind SLTT agencies directly; obligation 10 (civil fine) and obligation 12 (the FCC section 333 exemption) are the two most workspace-adjacent items for a vendor or venue-support workspace, since they define the penalty exposure an SLTT partner faces and the legal-liability relief a workspace's own RF-emitting equipment can claim when operated under an SLTT agency's authority.

*Per the workspace's reading:* no source in this brief's corpus states a compliance deadline, fine, or civil penalty running directly to a freight forwarder, vendor, or venue operator under 6 U.S.C. 124n; every penalty and enforcement mechanism surveyed above (obligations 9-11) runs to the SLTT agency exercising C-UAS authority.

Obligations surveyed: 12; workspace-adjacent: 12; extracted as FACT: 12.

# 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*This section applies where the workspace supplies C-UAS technology products or systems to SLTT agencies.*

FACT: "Detection and warning activity conducted using systems that do not require the authority of 6 U.S.C. 124n (including, for example, electro-optical, infrared, acoustic sensors, and radar) is not subject to this part." *Source: Federal Register document 2026-13609, DHS/DOJ, July 6, 2026, 6 CFR 124.2. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/06/2026-13609/counter-uas-authority-for-state-local-tribal-and-territorial-law-enforcement-and-correctional

*Operational implication:* this is a competitive differentiator for vendors of passive systems, which face no ATL/ASL gate and no per-operation FCC authorization requirement for non-emitting systems.

FACT: "issued an Order waiving the FCC’s equipment authorization rules to allow manufacturers and vendors to market and import, and SLTT law enforcement and correctional agencies to operate, counter-unmanned aircraft systems (C-UAS) equipment that is included on the SAFER SKIES Act’s Authorized Systems List prior to such equipment receiving an FCC equipment authorization." *Source: FCC Fact Sheet DOC-422788A1, FCC, July 2, 2026. https://docs.fcc.gov/public/attachments/DOC-422788A1.pdf

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a specific product's technical characteristics qualify it for a given Authorized Technologies List category, and whether the FCC equipment-authorization waiver applies to that specific product, requires both technical assessment against ATL category definitions and counsel review of the waiver's scope.

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

FACT: "the NCUTC certification database, which is the system of record for all certifications issued under this section." *Source: Federal Register document 2026-13609, DHS/DOJ, July 6, 2026, 6 CFR 124.5(c). https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/06/2026-13609/counter-uas-authority-for-state-local-tribal-and-territorial-law-enforcement-and-correctional

FACT: "Each agency must maintain a roster of its certified personnel drawn from the NCUTC certification database and must verify the certification status of personnel assigned to C-UAS operations." *Source: Federal Register document 2026-13609, DHS/DOJ, July 6, 2026, 6 CFR 124.5(c). https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/06/2026-13609/counter-uas-authority-for-state-local-tribal-and-territorial-law-enforcement-and-correctional

*Operational implication:* an SLTT agency's registration and reporting obligations run through the NCUTC certification database and the Federal C-UAS coordination portal; a workspace supporting an accredited agency under a mutual-aid arrangement (Section 7) does not itself register in either system.

# 11. Operational System Requirements

FACT: the audit trail "must be searchable and accessible to compliance auditors, protected against unauthorized modification or deletion, and retained for a minimum of 6 years." *Source: Federal Register document 2026-13609, DHS/DOJ, July 6, 2026, 6 CFR 124.14(g). https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/06/2026-13609/counter-uas-authority-for-state-local-tribal-and-territorial-law-enforcement-and-correctional

FACT: "Data purge verification means documented confirmation that records subject to purge have been deleted from all systems on which they were stored." *Source: Federal Register document 2026-13609, DHS/DOJ, July 6, 2026, 6 CFR 124.2. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/06/2026-13609/counter-uas-authority-for-state-local-tribal-and-territorial-law-enforcement-and-correctional

*Operational implication:* for a workspace whose facility or venue security systems interoperate with an SLTT agency's C-UAS data handling, the 6-year audit-trail retention and documented purge-verification requirements set the baseline records infrastructure the partnering agency must already satisfy.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

FACT: "This part does not affect the authority of any law enforcement or correctional officer to take physical custody of an unmanned aircraft or UAS under traditional law enforcement authority independent of 6 U.S.C. 124n." *Source: Federal Register document 2026-13609, DHS/DOJ, July 6, 2026, 6 CFR 124.17(a)(2). https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/06/2026-13609/counter-uas-authority-for-state-local-tribal-and-territorial-law-enforcement-and-correctional

FACT: "The physical act of interception of a third-party unmanned aircraft while it is in flight, such as catching or netting an aircraft by hand or using a non-electronic physical device to capture it in the air, implicates 6 U.S.C. 124n(b)(1)(D), (E), or (F). Personnel conducting such actions must therefore hold a Mitigation Certification." *Source: Federal Register document 2026-13609, DHS/DOJ, July 6, 2026, 6 CFR 124.17(a)(7). https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/06/2026-13609/counter-uas-authority-for-state-local-tribal-and-territorial-law-enforcement-and-correctional

FACT: "This does not apply to the erection of physical barriers that a drone operator has an obligation to avoid, such as netting affixed to a physical structure." *Source: Federal Register document 2026-13609, DHS/DOJ, July 6, 2026, 6 CFR 124.17(a)(7). https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/06/2026-13609/counter-uas-authority-for-state-local-tribal-and-territorial-law-enforcement-and-correctional

FACT: when "a credible threat poses an imminent risk to human life and advance coordination under this section is not practicable, an SLTT law enforcement or correctional agency may take mitigation action." *Source: Federal Register document 2026-13609, DHS/DOJ, July 6, 2026, 6 CFR 124.9(g). https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/06/2026-13609/counter-uas-authority-for-state-local-tribal-and-territorial-law-enforcement-and-correctional

FACT: this emergency exception "may not be invoked as a routine alternative to advance coordination, and a pattern of repeated invocations may result in compliance review under Sec. 124.16, accreditation or certification suspension, and penalties under section 8605(f) of the SAFER SKIES Act." *Source: Federal Register document 2026-13609, DHS/DOJ, July 6, 2026, 6 CFR 124.9(g). https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/06/2026-13609/counter-uas-authority-for-state-local-tribal-and-territorial-law-enforcement-and-correctional

*Analytical inference:* the physical-barrier exception (netting affixed to a structure) is the edge case most likely to matter for a freight-handling or venue-perimeter workspace, since it distinguishes ordinary perimeter fencing/netting from an in-flight interception device that would require Mitigation Certification.

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

*Section note: no peer-reviewed research on SAFER SKIES Act implementation outcomes exists as of this brief; the Act was signed December 18, 2025 and the IFR became effective July 1, 2026. The following is practitioner analysis and government-stated context from the captured corpus.*

FACT: "The National Football League's chief security officer told Congress in December 2024 that unauthorized drone incursions into the restricted airspace over NFL games grew from roughly a dozen in the 2017 season to 2,537 in 2022 and 2,845 in 2023." *Source: Federal Register document 2026-13609, DHS/DOJ, July 6, 2026, preamble. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/06/2026-13609/counter-uas-authority-for-state-local-tribal-and-territorial-law-enforcement-and-correctional

FACT: "DHS, through the Federal Emergency Management Agency (``FEMA''), noticed and awarded $250 million in Federal funding in FY 2026 to enhance SLTT agency capabilities to detect, identify, track, or monitor UAS in anticipation of the FIFA World Cup" *Source: Federal Register document 2026-13609, DHS/DOJ, July 6, 2026, preamble. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/06/2026-13609/counter-uas-authority-for-state-local-tribal-and-territorial-law-enforcement-and-correctional

*Operational implication:* for C-UAS technology vendors, the FEMA grant program is a funded demand signal; agencies receiving FY 2026 grant dollars are already required to have members enrolled in NCUTC training per grant conditions.

FACT: "that section 333 does not apply to federal government entities, and that non-federal parties, including SLTT authorities or federal contractors, testing or operating C-UAS signal jamming on behalf of or under the oversight of the federal government will similarly not be liable under section 333." *Source: FCC Fact Sheet DOC-422788A1, FCC, July 2, 2026. https://docs.fcc.gov/public/attachments/DOC-422788A1.pdf

*Industry interpretation:* this declaratory ruling removes a legal barrier that had created uncertainty about whether RF-based C-UAS mitigation by non-federal entities could expose operators to Communications Act liability; vendors and counsel relying on it should confirm its precise scope through independent legal review, as declaratory rulings can be revisited.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- December 18, 2025: SAFER SKIES Act signed into law, starting the 180-day statutory rulemaking clock.
- July 1, 2026: Interim Final Rule effective date; SLTT agencies may begin seeking accreditation and conducting operations under 6 U.S.C. 124n(a)(2).
- July 2, 2026: FCC releases its coordinated fact sheet and companion actions (equipment-authorization waiver, blanket 180-day Special Temporary Authority, section 333 declaratory rulings).
- July 6, 2026: Interim Final Rule published in the Federal Register (Vol. 91, No. 127).
- September 4, 2026: Public comment period on the Interim Final Rule closes.
- September 29, 2026: deadline for previously NCUTC-certified mitigation personnel to complete the detection and warning online curriculum.
- December 31, 2031: statutory termination of SLTT C-UAS authority under 6 U.S.C. 124n(j)(2) absent further Congressional action.

*Source for timeline entries: Federal Register document 2026-13609, DHS/DOJ, July 6, 2026 (https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/06/2026-13609/counter-uas-authority-for-state-local-tribal-and-territorial-law-enforcement-and-correctional); FCC Fact Sheet DOC-422788A1, FCC, July 2, 2026 (https://docs.fcc.gov/public/attachments/DOC-422788A1.pdf).*

FACT: "Personnel holding a Mitigation Certification issued by the NCUTC before the effective date of this part must complete the detection and warning curriculum under paragraph (c) of this section by September 29, 2026." *Source: Federal Register document 2026-13609, DHS/DOJ, July 6, 2026, 6 CFR 124.5(n). https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/06/2026-13609/counter-uas-authority-for-state-local-tribal-and-territorial-law-enforcement-and-correctional

*Operational implication:* this transition deadline applies only to personnel already Mitigation-Certified before the IFR's own effective date; their Mitigation Certification stays valid while they complete the online curriculum.

FACT: "Absent additional statutory authority, the authority of SLTT law enforcement and correctional agencies and their personnel under 6 U.S.C. 124n(a)(2) will terminate on December 31, 2031, as provided in 6 U.S.C. 124n(j)(2)." *Source: Federal Register document 2026-13609, DHS/DOJ, July 6, 2026, 6 CFR 124.21(a). https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/06/2026-13609/counter-uas-authority-for-state-local-tribal-and-territorial-law-enforcement-and-correctional
