entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks China's national carbon Emissions Trading System (ETS) as reshaped by the "Opinions on Advancing Green and Low-Carbon Transformation and Strengthening the Construction of the National ETS" (the "Opinions", issued August 25, 2025), a policy guideline jointly issued by the General Office of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and the General Office of the State Council. It exists to give a freight forwarder with China air-freight or China-entity exposure a single place to see: what the Opinions commit China's ETS to over 2027 and 2030, which sectors are currently covered, and what forward-looking signals bear on aviation's potential future inclusion.

FACT: "On August 25, 2025, the General Office of the Central Committee of the Chinese Communist Party (CCP), the CCP’s decision-making body, and the General Office of the State Council, the State Council’s administrative organ, released a new set of opinions to expand China’s carbon trading market in pursuit of lower-carbon development." *Source: China Briefing, October 2, 2025.* https://www.china-briefing.com/news/china-carbon-trading-emissions-cap/

FACT: "The guideline calls for expanding the coverage of the national carbon trading market." *Source: www.gov.cn, August 25, 2025.* https://english.www.gov.cn/policies/latestreleases/202508/25/content_WS68ac6afac6d0868f4e8f50fc.html

*Analytical inference:* The Opinions are a policy guideline directing the Ministry of Ecology and Environment (MEE) to develop implementing rules, not a self-executing statute with its own compliance deadlines running to private parties; the workspace-relevant content is therefore the trajectory the Opinions set for the ETS and CCER markets, not a direct duty on a freight forwarder.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The Opinions apply to the workspace indirectly at present: the ETS does not yet cover aviation or road transport, so no freight-forwarding activity is a currently covered emissions source. The Opinions matter because they set the 2027 and 2030 horizon at which additional sectors, potentially including aviation, may be added, and because carbon costs already passed through by covered Chinese counterparties (steel, cement, aluminum, power) can appear in shipment-adjacent pricing.

FACT: "The guideline is jointly issued by the General Office of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and the General Office of the State Council." *Source: www.gov.cn, August 25, 2025.* https://english.www.gov.cn/policies/latestreleases/202508/25/content_WS68ac6afac6d0868f4e8f50fc.html

FACT: "The country is aiming to encompass all major industrial sectors in the carbon trading market by 2027, while the national voluntary greenhouse gas emission reduction trading market is expected to expand to include all key fields, according to a guideline unveiled in August." *Source: www.gov.cn, January 2, 2026.* https://english.www.gov.cn/archive/statistics/202601/02/content_WS6957198ac6d00ca5f9a0860e.html

*Operational implication:* A workspace with China-touching air freight should track this 2027 horizon as the trigger point for potential aviation inclusion, rather than treating the current ETS scope as fixed.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

FACT: "Starting as early as 2027, sectors with relatively stable emissions profiles will be subject to absolute cap controls. At that point, increases in production by covered entities will no longer automatically result in higher allowance allocations." *Source: ICAP, September 29, 2025.* https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/news/china-issues-landmark-guidelines-transition-absolute-cap-and-expand-scope-national-ets

*Operational implication:* The near-term action item is monitoring, not compliance: the workspace should track MEE sector-designation announcements and Opinions implementing rules as the trigger events, since neither has yet named aviation or road transport as a covered sector.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

*Legal Confirmation Required:* If the workspace operates any China-domiciled entity in the power, steel, cement, or aluminum sectors, or a sector added to the ETS in the future, the following applies and requires legal confirmation:

FACT: "The ETS covers key emissions units, companies whose annual greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions exceed 26,000 tons of CO2 equivalent (CO2e)." *Source: China Briefing, October 2, 2025.* https://www.china-briefing.com/news/china-carbon-trading-emissions-cap/

FACT: "These entities are responsible for controlling their emissions, reporting verified carbon data, surrendering allowances, disclosing trading activity, and complying with oversight from provincial and national ecological and environmental authorities." *Source: China Briefing, October 2, 2025.* https://www.china-briefing.com/news/china-carbon-trading-emissions-cap/ *Operational implication:* these obligations run to the covered Chinese entity itself, not to a freight forwarder handling that entity's cargo, unless the workspace itself operates a covered China entity.

*Analytical inference:* Because the ETS's compliance chain currently runs from a covered domestic emitter to the MEE and provincial/national environmental authorities, a freight forwarder's practical exposure today is indirect (carbon cost pass-through, forward planning for aviation) rather than a direct reporting duty.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: "The guideline calls for invigorating the carbon trading market by enriching trading products, expanding market participants, and strengthening market supervision." *Source: www.gov.cn, August 25, 2025.* https://english.www.gov.cn/policies/latestreleases/202508/25/content_WS68ac6afac6d0868f4e8f50fc.html

FACT: "improving carbon emission accounting and reporting as well as enhancing the information disclosure system." *Source: www.gov.cn, August 25, 2025.* https://english.www.gov.cn/policies/latestreleases/202508/25/content_WS68ac6afac6d0868f4e8f50fc.html *Operational implication:* enhanced information-disclosure requirements for covered entities will require more granular MRV data as the ETS expands, which is the same mechanism that would eventually apply to aviation if that sector is added.

*Per the workspace's reading:* the Opinions are the controlling policy instrument for the 2027/2030 trajectory analyzed in this brief; they direct the MEE to develop supporting implementing rules that will carry the operative legal detail once published.

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

1. **2027 (high confidence).** FACT: "The country is aiming to encompass all major industrial sectors in the carbon trading market by 2027, while the national voluntary greenhouse gas emission reduction trading market is expected to expand to include all key fields, according to a guideline unveiled in August." *Source: www.gov.cn, January 2, 2026.* https://english.www.gov.cn/archive/statistics/202601/02/content_WS6957198ac6d00ca5f9a0860e.html *Operational implication:* this is the headline forward event this brief tracks; no MEE implementing rule naming the newly included sectors had been published as of this capture.

2. **2027 (medium confidence, workspace-authored operational implication, not a source quote).** *Operational implication:* A workspace managing China-origin or China-destination air freight without route-level GHG data capture is not positioned to satisfy a potential ETS reporting obligation if aviation is included by 2027; building a China-routes carbon accounting capability ahead of that date is a forward-planning action, not a current compliance requirement.

3. **2030 (medium confidence).** FACT: "the allocation mechanism will evolve from primarily free allocation to a hybrid model incorporating auctioning of allowances." *Source: ICAP, September 29, 2025.* https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/news/china-issues-landmark-guidelines-transition-absolute-cap-and-expand-scope-national-ets

4. **2030 (medium confidence).** FACT: "By 2030, China aims to have a cap-and-trade system with a mix of allocation and auctioning." *Source: ICAP, September 29, 2025.* https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/news/china-issues-landmark-guidelines-transition-absolute-cap-and-expand-scope-national-ets

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this brief's own corpus does not include the Opinions' own full Chinese-language legal text, only English-language government and third-party analysis of it; a workspace with a specific compliance question should confirm current status directly with MEE or qualified China counsel rather than relying solely on this summary.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Is aviation formally designated as an ETS-covered sector?**

*Analytical inference:* Not yet. FACT: "civil aviation, copper smelting, flat glass, petrochemicals, chemicals, and paper manufacturing have already undergone a decade of greenhouse gas data monitoring, reporting, and verification (MRV)." *Source: ICAP, September 29, 2025.* https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/news/china-issues-landmark-guidelines-transition-absolute-cap-and-expand-scope-national-ets Being MRV-ready is not the same as being formally designated; no source in this corpus states that aviation has been added to the ETS.

**Q2: Does the workspace operate any China-based entity exceeding the key-emitter threshold?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* FACT: "The ETS covers key emissions units, companies whose annual greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions exceed 26,000 tons of CO2 equivalent (CO2e)." *Source: China Briefing, October 2, 2025.* https://www.china-briefing.com/news/china-carbon-trading-emissions-cap/ Whether any workspace entity meets this threshold requires legal review.

**Q3: Does the workspace's China air-freight volume require ETS-compliance tracking now?**

*Analytical inference:* Not yet mandatory under any source in this corpus; forward planning is advised given the 2027 horizon discussed in Section 6.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

## Currently in force

**1. Key-emitter registration and quota management (power, steel, cement, aluminum).** FACT: "In 2025, a total of 3,378 key emitters were included in the carbon emission trading market's quota management, including 2,087 emitters from the power generation sector, 232 from the steel sector, 962 from the cement sector, and 97 from the aluminum smelting sector." *Source: www.gov.cn, January 2, 2026.* https://english.www.gov.cn/archive/statistics/202601/02/content_WS6957198ac6d00ca5f9a0860e.html *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any workspace entity is a "key emitter" in these sectors requires legal review.

**2. Key-emitter threshold and jurisdictional scope.** FACT: "The ETS covers key emissions units, companies whose annual greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions exceed 26,000 tons of CO2 equivalent (CO2e)." *Source: China Briefing, October 2, 2025.* https://www.china-briefing.com/news/china-carbon-trading-emissions-cap/

**3. MRV, allowance-surrender, and disclosure obligations for covered entities.** FACT: "These entities are responsible for controlling their emissions, reporting verified carbon data, surrendering allowances, disclosing trading activity, and complying with oversight from provincial and national ecological and environmental authorities." *Source: China Briefing, October 2, 2025.* https://www.china-briefing.com/news/china-carbon-trading-emissions-cap/ *Operational implication:* these obligations run to the covered Chinese entity, not to a freight forwarder acting as its logistics provider.

**4. Current allocation method for the power sector (free, efficiency-benchmarked).** FACT: "companies in the power generation sector have received free CEAs based on their electricity and heat output and government-set efficiency benchmarks." *Source: China Briefing, October 2, 2025.* https://www.china-briefing.com/news/china-carbon-trading-emissions-cap/

**5. 2024 allocation method for cement, steel, and aluminum (free, verified-emissions basis).** FACT: "In 2024, the first year of their inclusion in the ETS, companies in the cement, steel, and aluminum smelting sectors received allowances based on verified emissions." *Source: China Briefing, October 2, 2025.* https://www.china-briefing.com/news/china-carbon-trading-emissions-cap/

**6. 2025-2026 allocation transition for cement, steel, and aluminum (intensity-based, output-tied).** FACT: "For the 2025 to 2026 period, allocation will shift to an intensity-based approach tied to production output." *Source: China Briefing, October 2, 2025.* https://www.china-briefing.com/news/china-carbon-trading-emissions-cap/

## Forthcoming (announced; not yet in force)

**7. Primary 2027 expansion deadline.** FACT: "by 2027, the country's carbon trading market will encompass all major industrial sectors." *Source: www.gov.cn, August 25, 2025.* https://english.www.gov.cn/policies/latestreleases/202508/25/content_WS68ac6afac6d0868f4e8f50fc.html

**8. Absolute-cap transition (2027, sector-conditional).** FACT: "Starting as early as 2027, sectors with relatively stable emissions profiles will be subject to absolute cap controls. At that point, increases in production by covered entities will no longer automatically result in higher allowance allocations." *Source: ICAP, September 29, 2025.* https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/news/china-issues-landmark-guidelines-transition-absolute-cap-and-expand-scope-national-ets Qualification: the condition "relatively stable emissions profiles" is not yet elaborated in published implementing guidance.

**9. Orderly expansion of sector and gas coverage.** FACT: "The Opinions call for the orderly inclusion of additional sectors and greenhouse gases in the National ETS, guided by factors such as sectoral emissions, data quality, and abatement potential." *Source: ICAP, September 29, 2025.* https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/news/china-issues-landmark-guidelines-transition-absolute-cap-and-expand-scope-national-ets

**10. Shift to hybrid free-plus-auctioned allocation.** FACT: "the allocation mechanism will evolve from primarily free allocation to a hybrid model incorporating auctioning of allowances." *Source: ICAP, September 29, 2025.* https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/news/china-issues-landmark-guidelines-transition-absolute-cap-and-expand-scope-national-ets

**11. Allowance reserve and market-stability mechanism.** FACT: "A market reserve and adjustment mechanism will be established to stabilize carbon prices and balance supply and demand, drawing on successful experiences from regional pilots." *Source: ICAP, September 29, 2025.* https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/news/china-issues-landmark-guidelines-transition-absolute-cap-and-expand-scope-national-ets

**12. 2030 cap-and-trade / mixed-allocation target.** FACT: "By 2030, China aims to have a cap-and-trade system with a mix of allocation and auctioning." *Source: ICAP, September 29, 2025.* https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/news/china-issues-landmark-guidelines-transition-absolute-cap-and-expand-scope-national-ets

**13. Enhanced information-disclosure requirement.** FACT: "Emitters, registries, exchanges, and financial institutions must disclose emissions, trading, and compliance data." *Source: Climate Cooperation China, October 28, 2025.* https://climatecooperation.cn/climate/china-unveils-roadmap-for-absolute-emission-caps-2027-and-2030-milestones-for-national-carbon-markets/ *Operational implication:* freight forwarders managing China carbon-credit positions or acting as agents for covered emitters may face new data-provision or disclosure requirements as the system expands.

**14. Coverage growth as scope evidence.** FACT: "bringing 1,334 additional emitting entities under its scope and raising coverage of the country’s total carbon emissions from 40% to 60%." *Source: IEEFA, November 3, 2025.* https://ieefa.org/resources/chinas-emissions-trading-system-ets-reforms-track-needs-robust-enforcement *Analytical inference:* this is the same 2024 sectoral expansion described in obligations 5 and 6 above, restated from the coverage-share angle.

No exceptions are stated in Sections covering ETS scope expansion, allowance allocation, and CCER development.

Obligations surveyed: 14; workspace-adjacent: 14; extracted as FACT: 14.

# 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

FACT: "As the ETS expands to cover all major emitting industries by 2027, foreign firms in sectors that could be affected, in particular petrochemicals, nonferrous metals, and aviation, will come under the purview of the ETS." *Source: China Briefing, October 2, 2025.* https://www.china-briefing.com/news/china-carbon-trading-emissions-cap/ *Operational implication:* freight-forwarding activity itself is not a product covered by the ETS today; the product-specific exposure identified in this corpus is for foreign firms operating covered-sector entities in China, not for logistics services.

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

## Currently applicable to covered sectors (not currently transportation)

FACT: "These entities are responsible for controlling their emissions, reporting verified carbon data, surrendering allowances, disclosing trading activity, and complying with oversight from provincial and national ecological and environmental authorities." *Source: China Briefing, October 2, 2025.* https://www.china-briefing.com/news/china-carbon-trading-emissions-cap/

FACT: "Emitters, registries, exchanges, and financial institutions must disclose emissions, trading, and compliance data." *Source: Climate Cooperation China, October 28, 2025.* https://climatecooperation.cn/climate/china-unveils-roadmap-for-absolute-emission-caps-2027-and-2030-milestones-for-national-carbon-markets/ *Operational implication:* no source in this corpus names a registration or reporting obligation running to a freight forwarder itself.

# 11. Operational System Requirements

*Note: because no source in this corpus states an operational-system requirement running to a freight forwarder today, this section records the monitoring infrastructure a workspace should maintain rather than a system the regulation itself requires.*

*Operational implication:* A workspace managing China-origin or China-destination air freight should begin route-level GHG data capture now, ahead of the 2027 horizon discussed in Section 6, so a full baseline year exists before any compliance cycle could begin.

*Operational implication:* A workspace should monitor MEE announcements and Opinions implementing rules for formal sector designation, since neither source in this corpus states that aviation or road transport has been added.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

FACT: "The ETS covers key emissions units, companies whose annual greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions exceed 26,000 tons of CO2 equivalent (CO2e)." *Source: China Briefing, October 2, 2025.* https://www.china-briefing.com/news/china-carbon-trading-emissions-cap/ *Analytical inference:* an entity below this threshold is not classified as a key emitter and is not currently subject to ETS quota management.

FACT: "Provincial pilot markets will continue to coordinate with the national ETS, with no new pilots planned." *Source: Climate Cooperation China, October 28, 2025.* https://climatecooperation.cn/climate/china-unveils-roadmap-for-absolute-emission-caps-2027-and-2030-milestones-for-national-carbon-markets/ *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a specific workspace-related entity operating in one of the eight regional pilot cities is governed by pilot rules or the national ETS requires confirmation with the relevant provincial authority.

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

FACT: "raise the share of national carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions covered by the market from 40% of China’s total to 60%, according to the MEE." *Source: Carbon Brief, September 23, 2024.* https://www.carbonbrief.org/explainer-chinas-carbon-market-to-cover-steel-aluminium-and-cement-in-2024

FACT: "afforestation, solar thermal power, offshore wind power, mangrove creation, energy-saving highway tunnel lighting systems, low-concentration coal mine gas, wind exhaust gas utilization, biomass power generation, and oil and gas methane recovery from onshore and offshore oilfields." *Source: China Briefing, October 2, 2025.* https://www.china-briefing.com/news/china-carbon-trading-emissions-cap/ *Analytical inference:* the CCER voluntary-offset program is the domestic mechanism most relevant to a workspace seeking China-linked carbon-neutrality claims, distinct from the mandatory ETS discussed in Section 8.

FACT: "The EU ETS’s LRF started at 1.74% in 2013." *Source: IEEFA, November 3, 2025.* https://ieefa.org/resources/chinas-emissions-trading-system-ets-reforms-track-needs-robust-enforcement *Analytical inference:* IEEFA's own analysis uses the EU ETS's linear reduction factor as the benchmark China's own absolute-cap design should emulate; this is comparator context, not a China ETS requirement.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- July 2021: China's national ETS launched, covering the power sector only.
- 2024: ETS coverage expanded to steel, cement, and aluminum; roughly 1,334 new entities added; national emissions coverage raised from about 40% to about 60%.
- August 25, 2025: the Opinions on Advancing Green and Low-Carbon Transformation and Strengthening the Construction of the National ETS issued, setting the 2027/2030 roadmap analyzed in this brief.
- 2026: EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) enters full enforcement, a comparator pricing pressure discussed in Section 13.
- 2027: ETS target to encompass all major industrial sectors (forthcoming; implementing rules pending).
- 2027: absolute-cap controls target start date for sectors with relatively stable emissions profiles (forthcoming; condition definition pending).
- 2027: CCER voluntary market target to expand to cover all key fields (forthcoming).
- 2030: national ETS target to transition to a cap-and-trade system mixing free and paid allocations (forthcoming).
- 2030: voluntary CCER market target for credibility, transparency, broad participation, and international standard alignment (forthcoming).
- 2030: China's national peak-carbon-emissions commitment.
- 2060: China's national carbon-neutrality commitment.

FACT: "China officially launched its national carbon emissions trading market in July 2021, which has since evolved into the world's largest carbon market in terms of total greenhouse gas emissions traded." *Source: www.gov.cn, January 2, 2026.* https://english.www.gov.cn/archive/statistics/202601/02/content_WS6957198ac6d00ca5f9a0860e.html

FACT: "The trading volume of carbon emission quotas reached 235 million tonnes last year, marking an increase of 24 percent year on year." *Source: www.gov.cn, January 2, 2026.* https://english.www.gov.cn/archive/statistics/202601/02/content_WS6957198ac6d00ca5f9a0860e.html

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Japan's Green Transformation (GX) League framework and the GX-ETS emissions trading system nested within it, as they apply to freight transport operations. "GX League" is the voluntary framework launched in FY2023 under the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI); "GX-ETS" is the emissions trading system evolving from it. Phase 1 (FY2023-FY2025) is voluntary; Phase 2 (FY2026-FY2032) is mandatory; Phase 3 (from FY2033) introduces auctioning for the power sector. Monetary figures below are Japanese Yen (JPY) unless otherwise noted.

FACT: "The GX League is a framework in which a group of internationally competitive companies that are boldly taking on the challenge of transitioning to carbon neutrality will drive GX." *Source: From FY2024, 179 Companies Newly Participate in the GX League, METI, 27 March 2024. https://www.meti.go.jp/english/press/2024/0327_003.html

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "Jurisdictions Japan Sectoral coverage Maritime Domestic Aviation Transport Industry Power" *Source: Japan GX-ETS, ICAP. https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/ets/japan-gx-ets

FACT: "Japan started its GX-ETS as a voluntary baseline-and-credit system during its first phase spanning FY2023 and FY2025." *Source: Japan GX-ETS, ICAP. https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/ets/japan-gx-ets

FACT: "In the FY2026, which started in April 2026, the GX-ETS transitioned to a mandatory baseline-and-credit system." *Source: Japan GX-ETS, ICAP. https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/ets/japan-gx-ets

*Operational implication:* the covered entity under Phase 2 is most likely the carrier operating freight automobile, domestic marine, or air transport, not the freight forwarder or shipper directly, unless the forwarder itself operates covered transport assets.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any role the workspace occupies (freight forwarder, importer, logistics coordinator) constitutes a "covered entity" under the amended GX Promotion Act, or whether compliance obligations pass through contractually from carrier to customer, requires counsel review.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

*Operational implication:* the mandatory Phase 2 obligation began in April 2026 (Section 14); a workspace with Japan transport-lane exposure should confirm now whether its own operations or its carrier partners' operations meet the inclusion threshold below.

FACT: "Companies with annual CO 2 emissions of 100,000 tonnes or more in power, industry, transport and aviation as well as in other sectors if their annual CO 2  emissions exceed the 100,000 tonnes threshold." *Source: Japan GX-ETS, ICAP. https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/ets/japan-gx-ets

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a freight forwarder or logistics operator acting on behalf of carrier clients meets this threshold, or whether obligations pass through to the freight principal, requires counsel review and cannot be determined from the sourced materials alone.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The GX League and GX-ETS are company-level frameworks; covered entities are companies meeting emissions thresholds, not cargo principals or freight forwarders acting as intermediaries per se.

FACT: "Freight automobile transportation •    Domestic marine transportation •    Air transportation" *Source: Japan GX-ETS, ICAP. https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/ets/japan-gx-ets

*Operational implication:* carrier compliance costs under the GX-ETS (allowance purchases, MRV costs) are likely to be incorporated into freight pricing on Japan lanes over FY2026-FY2032; workspace clients operating under CSRD, ISSB, or equivalent disclosure frameworks may separately request Japan transport emissions data at carrier-activity level for Scope 3 accounting.

FACT: "active discussions on and proposals for rulemaking, which is difficult for individual companies to undertake, have been held regarding areas such as emissions reductions throughout the supply chain and the input of green products into the market." *Source: From FY2024, 179 Companies Newly Participate in the GX League, METI, 27 March 2024. https://www.meti.go.jp/english/press/2024/0327_003.html

FACT: "the NYK Group set a long-term goal of reducing greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions in the Group’s oceangoing shipping business to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050" *Source: NYK to Join Japanese Ministry's GX League, NYK Line, 9 June 2023. https://www.nyk.com/english/news/2023/20230607_01.html

*Operational implication:* ocean carrier partners on Japan trade lanes who are GX League participants are subject to self-set emission-reduction targets today and, from Phase 2, mandatory compliance obligations; Japan-lane ocean freight procurement should factor in carrier compliance posture.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: "A place where companies actively engaged in GX are invited to collaborate with government, academia, and financial institutions to take up the challenge of GX, and engage in discussions for the transformation of the entire economic and social system and the creation of new markets." *Source: NYK to Join Japanese Ministry's GX League, NYK Line, 9 June 2023 (quoting METI's GX League Basic Concept). https://www.nyk.com/english/news/2023/20230607_01.html

FACT: "In May 2025, the amended GX Promotion Act (Officially named as: Bill for the Act for Partially Amending the Act on the Promoting Transition to the Decarbonized Growth Economic Structure and Act on the Promotion of Effective Utilization of Resources) was passed and enacted at the House of Councillors plenary session, obliging companies that emit at least 100,000 metric tons of carbon dioxide a year to participate in the emissions trading system to be introduced in fiscal (FY) 2026." *Source: GX-ETS Phase 2, InfluenceMap, December 2025. https://japan.influencemap.org/policy/GX-ETS-Phase-2-5560

*Operational implication:* the amended GX Promotion Act is the binding statutory instrument for Phase 2; GX League membership is the voluntary, reputational, supply-chain-facing predecessor structure, distinct from statutory GX-ETS compliance.

FACT: "REPORTING:  Covered entities must submit their emissions reports annually by January 31 of the year following the reporting year." *Source: Japan GX-ETS, ICAP. https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/ets/japan-gx-ets

FACT: "VERIFICATION:  Emissions reports require third-party verification by an accredited verifier." *Source: Japan GX-ETS, ICAP. https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/ets/japan-gx-ets

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

FACT: "On December 19, 2025, the subcommittee released its final report and requested that the Minister of Economy, Trade and Industry establish the Reference Upper Limit Transaction Price and the Adjustment Standard Transaction Price based on the following opinions: For fiscal year 2026, the Reference Upper Limit Transaction Price shall be set at 4,300 yen per carbon-dioxide-emission-quota unit for decarbonized growth-oriented investment, which is equivalent to one ton of CO2 emissions." *Source: GX-ETS Phase 2, InfluenceMap, December 2025. https://japan.influencemap.org/policy/GX-ETS-Phase-2-5560

FACT: "For the period from fiscal year 2027 to fiscal year 2030, the Reference Upper Limit Transaction Price and the Adjustment Standard Transaction Price shall be updated and determined annually in accordance with the law; these prices shall be adjusted by applying a 3% increase to the projected consumer price index for the relevant fiscal year, using the price of the previous fiscal year as the baseline." *Source: GX-ETS Phase 2, InfluenceMap, December 2025. https://japan.influencemap.org/policy/GX-ETS-Phase-2-5560

*Operational implication:* resolution of banking rules in FY2027 (Section 8) will affect allowance-management strategy for covered transport-sector entities; workspace carrier partners should be asked about allowance position and banking exposure once rules are finalized.

FACT: "a carbon levy (GX-Surcharge) to be introduced from 2028 on fossil fuel importers and domestic fossil fuel extractors." *Source: Japan GX-ETS, ICAP. https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/ets/japan-gx-ets

*Operational implication:* the GX-Surcharge, once introduced in FY2028, is a distinct, additional carbon-pricing layer on fossil fuel costs for Japan transport operators, separate from GX-ETS allowance costs.

FACT: "From FY2033, auctioning will be introduced for high-emitting corporations in the power sector." *Source: Japan GX-ETS, ICAP. https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/ets/japan-gx-ets

*Analytical inference:* auctioning is currently scoped to the power sector only; no sourced evidence places transport-sector auctioning on the current Phase 2 (FY2026-FY2032) policy trajectory.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Is the workspace a "covered entity" under Phase 2?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* Phase 2 coverage turns on whether a company's annual CO2 emissions meet or exceed the 100,000-tonne threshold under the amended GX Promotion Act (Section 3). Whether freight forwarding or logistics coordination activity itself generates emissions meeting this threshold, or whether the threshold applies only to the asset operator, requires counsel and emissions-accounting review.

**Q2: Does the workspace's transport mode trigger transport-sector benchmarking?**

FACT: benchmarking applies to "Freight automobile transportation •    Domestic marine transportation •    Air transportation" *Source: Japan GX-ETS, ICAP. https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/ets/japan-gx-ets

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the workspace or its carrier partners fall into one of these named benchmark categories, or into the residual grandfathering category, requires assessment against actual transport operations and legal review.

**Q3: Does voluntary Phase 1 non-registration carry consequences?**

FACT: "The GX League will consider companies that have no intention to register their data and those that do not respond to the communications from the Secretariat as having withdrawn from the league as of the end of June 2024." *Source: From FY2024, 179 Companies Newly Participate in the GX League, METI, 27 March 2024. https://www.meti.go.jp/english/press/2024/0327_003.html

*Analytical inference:* this is a reputational/participation consequence, not a statutory penalty, in the Phase 1 voluntary period.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

**1. Phase 1 participation basis (voluntary).** FACT: "These companies have been making significant efforts to reduce emissions, upholding their own targets of emission reductions not only for FY2030 but also for FY2025, and have also decided to participate in an emissions trading system currently being operated on a trial basis." *Source: From FY2024, 179 Companies Newly Participate in the GX League, METI, 27 March 2024. https://www.meti.go.jp/english/press/2024/0327_003.html

**2. Phase 1 data registration.** FACT: "The GX League asks participants to register related data such as their emissions reduction targets." *Source: From FY2024, 179 Companies Newly Participate in the GX League, METI, 27 March 2024. https://www.meti.go.jp/english/press/2024/0327_003.html

**3. *Per the workspace's reading:* no source in this brief's corpus states a penalty running directly to a freight forwarder, importer, or logistics coordinator; every penalty and compliance-cost mechanism above (obligations 11-14) runs to the "covered entity" as defined by the amended GX Promotion Act, which the sourced materials define by direct CO2 emissions volume, not by commercial intermediary role.

# 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*This section applies where the workspace itself operates covered transport assets in Japan (freight automobile, domestic marine, or air transport) rather than acting purely as an intermediary.*

*Legal Confirmation Required:* if the workspace directly operates covered transport assets meeting the 100,000-tonne threshold (Section 8, obligation 4), it is itself a Phase 2 covered entity subject to the reporting, verification, and compliance-surrender obligations above; this determination requires counsel and emissions-accounting review on the workspace's specific asset operations.

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

FACT: "The GX League asks participants to register related data such as their emissions reduction targets." *Source: From FY2024, 179 Companies Newly Participate in the GX League, METI, 27 March 2024. https://www.meti.go.jp/english/press/2024/0327_003.html

FACT: "the GX League has opened a special consultation counter on its official website as a measure to support such companies in registering their data, which provides services such as tailored consultations, including explanations on how to calculate emissions." *Source: From FY2024, 179 Companies Newly Participate in the GX League, METI, 27 March 2024. https://www.meti.go.jp/english/press/2024/0327_003.html

FACT: "REPORTING:  Covered entities must submit their emissions reports annually by January 31 of the year following the reporting year. year." *Source: Japan GX-ETS, ICAP. https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/ets/japan-gx-ets

*Operational implication:* for workspace carrier partners who are Phase 2 covered entities, the annual reporting cycle (activity year to 31 January submission to third-party verification) creates a structured data-availability window; carrier-level data may not reach freight forwarders until the first quarter of the calendar year following the activity year.

# 11. Operational System Requirements

*Operational implication:* workspaces not directly covered should build capacity to request and receive verified CO2 data from Japan-based carrier partners, since this data underpins Scope 3 emissions reporting to clients operating under CSRD, ISSB, or equivalent disclosure frameworks.

FACT: emissions reports require "VERIFICATION:  Emissions reports require third-party verification by an accredited verifier." *Source: Japan GX-ETS, ICAP. https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/ets/japan-gx-ets

*Operational implication:* Phase 2 covered carrier partners will need to engage accredited verifiers, which is a procurement and lead-time consideration; workspace procurement teams should factor verifier availability into carrier readiness assessments.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

FACT: "The GX League will continue to provide meticulous support to participating companies, which vary in size and by industry, consisting of not only large enterprises but also SMEs and startups" *Source: From FY2024, 179 Companies Newly Participate in the GX League, METI, 27 March 2024. https://www.meti.go.jp/english/press/2024/0327_003.html

*Operational implication:* SME and startup freight operators voluntarily participating in the GX League have access to a special consultation counter and tailored support, reducing the barrier to voluntary participation for smaller transport operators.

FACT: "Banking: There are currently no regulations for banking in place, but the government is examining the possibility of implementing banking rules in FY2027. Borrowing is not allowed." *Source: Japan GX-ETS, ICAP. https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/ets/japan-gx-ets

*Analytical inference:* no banking is currently permitted and borrowing is not allowed at all; this is a scope limit on how covered entities may manage their compliance position across compliance periods.

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

FACT: "More than 700 companies, accounting for over 50% of national GHG emissions, participated in the voluntary ETS." *Source: Japan GX-ETS, ICAP. https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/ets/japan-gx-ets

*Analytical inference:* Japan Climate Initiative and Japan Climate Leaders Partnership are assessed as supporting GX-ETS Phase 2 with active and strategic engagement respectively, while Japan Iron and Steel Federation, Japan Chemical Industry Association, and Electric Power Development are characterised as not supporting, per InfluenceMap's policy-engagement tracker; transport-adjacent industry associations present a mixed-to-not-supporting position, which may shift benchmark and grandfathering design during Phase 2. *Source: GX-ETS Phase 2, InfluenceMap, December 2025. https://japan.influencemap.org/policy/GX-ETS-Phase-2-5560

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- February 1, 2022: GX League Basic Concept released by METI.
- FY2023: GX League launched; Phase 1 voluntary period opens.
- January 2024: call for FY2024 new GX League participants opened, including transport-sector companies.
- March 27, 2024: 179 new companies join, bringing total participants to 747.
- June 2024: METI treats non-responding FY2023 participants as withdrawn.
- May 2025: amended GX Promotion Act passed and enacted by the House of Councillors.
- July 2025: METI Subcommittee on Emissions Trading Systems holds its first meeting.
- December 19, 2025: METI Subcommittee releases its final report and sets the FY2026 price limits.
- April 2026: GX-ETS transitions to mandatory Phase 2.
- January 31, 2027: first Phase 2 MRV deadline, for FY2026 emissions.
- FY2027: banking rules under examination for potential introduction.
- FY2028: GX-Surcharge introduced on fossil fuel importers and domestic extractors.
- FY2033: Phase 3 begins; auctioning introduced for the power sector.
- 2050: net-zero GHG emissions target (Japan NDC).

*Source for timeline entries: From FY2024, 179 Companies Newly Participate in the GX League, METI, 27 March 2024 (https://www.meti.go.jp/english/press/2024/0327_003.html); Japan GX-ETS, ICAP (https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/ets/japan-gx-ets); GX-ETS Phase 2, InfluenceMap, December 2025 (https://japan.influencemap.org/policy/GX-ETS-Phase-2-5560); NYK to Join Japanese Ministry's GX League, NYK Line, 9 June 2023 (https://www.nyk.com/english/news/2023/20230607_01.html).*

FACT: "In January 2024, the GX League opened a call for new companies that intend to participate in the league from FY2024 and received applications." *Source: From FY2024, 179 Companies Newly Participate in the GX League, METI, 27 March 2024. https://www.meti.go.jp/english/press/2024/0327_003.html

FACT: "The first meeting was held in July 2025, and discussions are expected to conclude by the end of the year." *Source: GX-ETS Phase 2, InfluenceMap, December 2025. https://japan.influencemap.org/policy/GX-ETS-Phase-2-5560

FACT: "On December 19, 2025, the subcommittee released its final report and requested that the Minister of Economy, Trade and Industry establish the Reference Upper Limit Transaction Price and the Adjustment Standard Transaction Price based on the following opinions: For fiscal year 2026, the Reference Upper Limit Transaction Price shall be set at 4,300 yen per carbon-dioxide-emission-quota unit for decarbonized growth-oriented investment, which is equivalent to one ton of CO2 emissions." *Source: GX-ETS Phase 2, InfluenceMap, December 2025. https://japan.influencemap.org/policy/GX-ETS-Phase-2-5560

*Operational implication:* this final report is the design basis for the FY2026 price limits and the FY2027-FY2030 CPI-linked adjustment schedule (Section 8).

key_data: Phase 2 inclusion threshold 100000 tonnes CO2 per year

penalty for shortfall equals allowance shortfall times upper price times 1.1
offset credit cap 10 percent of compliance obligation
metadata.cost_mechanism: Covered entities surrender one compliance unit per tCO2 exceeding the facility's annual limit; a shortfall costs the shortfall volume multiplied by the upper price limit multiplied by 1.1, with the upper price itself acting as a cost ceiling.

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks the European Commission's proposal to revise the Weights and Dimensions Directive (Council Directive 96/53/EC), COM(2023) 445 final, currently in trilogue between the European Parliament, Council, and Commission. It exists to give a freight forwarder operating EU cross-border road legs a single place to see: the zero-emission-vehicle (ZEV) weight and length bonuses under negotiation, the 44-tonne cross-border facilitation and its proposed 2034 sunset, and the European Modular Systems (EMS) cross-border provisions.

FACT: "The legal basis for the proposed amending Directive is Article 91(1) of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union." *Source: COM(2023) 445 final.* https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:52023PC0445

FACT: "Directive 96/53/EC sets out maximum authorised weights and dimensions for HDVs that move on EU roads and carry goods or passengers." *Source: COM(2023) 445 final.* https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:52023PC0445

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this is a legislative PROPOSAL, not enacted law; every provision described in this brief is subject to change in trilogue, and the final directive text, once adopted, is the only source that legally binds Member States and, through their transposition, private operators.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "Strasbourg, 11.7.2023 COM(2023) 445 final" *Source: COM(2023) 445 final.* https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:52023PC0445

*Operational implication:* Once enacted and transposed, this directive will directly govern the maximum weights and dimensions of the HDVs a workspace's road-carrier partners operate on EU cross-border legs; today, it applies to the workspace only as a forward-planning signal, since the current directive (96/53/EC) remains in force unchanged.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

FACT: "The Council (Transport, Telecommunications and Energy) agreed on its general approach on 4 December 2025." *Source: European Parliament Legislative Train Schedule, as of the export date.* https://www.europarl.europa.eu/legislative-train/theme-a-european-green-deal/file-revision-of-the-weights-and-dimensions-directive

FACT: "Trilogue meetings started on 9 December 2025." *Source: European Parliament Legislative Train Schedule, as of the export date.* https://www.europarl.europa.eu/legislative-train/theme-a-european-green-deal/file-revision-of-the-weights-and-dimensions-directive

*Operational implication:* The near-term action item is monitoring, not compliance: trilogue is active and its outcome determines the final text; no compliance deadline has been triggered.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

*Legal Confirmation Required:* As proposed, this directive's compliance chain runs Member State to vehicle operator (the entity operating the HDV), not to a freight forwarder as a defined category. Whether a specific workspace entity is itself a vehicle operator, or acts only as an intermediary booking capacity from carriers, determines whether any future transposition measure applies directly.

*Analytical inference:* Because the directive's own scope is vehicles and their operators, a freight forwarder's practical exposure is through its carrier partners' compliance status (ZEV weight-bonus eligibility, EMS routing permissions, 44-tonne cross-border eligibility) rather than a direct duty running to the forwarder itself.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

*No content for this section as of the export date: the proposal remains in trilogue and has not been enacted, so no authoritative implementing or interpretive guidance document exists yet -- the corpus's own analytical commentary (EESC, IRU, Platform for Electromobility) is industry and advisory-body reaction to the legislative text, not authoritative guidance on an enacted instrument, and is treated as such throughout Sections 6-13 rather than cited here.*

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

## Trilogue negotiations -- ongoing

FACT: "Trilogue meetings started on 9 December 2025." *Source: European Parliament Legislative Train Schedule, as of the export date.* https://www.europarl.europa.eu/legislative-train/theme-a-european-green-deal/file-revision-of-the-weights-and-dimensions-directive

FACT: "The Council (Transport, Telecommunications and Energy) agreed on its general approach on 4 December 2025." *Source: European Parliament Legislative Train Schedule, as of the export date.* https://www.europarl.europa.eu/legislative-train/theme-a-european-green-deal/file-revision-of-the-weights-and-dimensions-directive

*Analytical inference:* No trilogue conclusion date is stated as a certainty anywhere in this corpus; industry commentary from the Platform for Electromobility expressed hope for a swift conclusion (see the sunset-clause FACT quote in Section 7), but this is advocacy, not a scheduled event.

## Expected subsequent regulatory events

Once the directive is enacted, a Member State transposition period will begin; *Analytical inference:* EU directives typically carry an 18-to-24-month transposition window, but the exact period will be set in the final directive text and cannot be confirmed from this corpus.

## Complementary regulatory events to monitor (Greening Freight Package)

FACT: "mely resident and non-resident offenders. In March 2023, the Commission adopted a legislative proposal 17 to amend" *Source: COM(2023) 445 final.* https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:52023PC0445 *Operational implication:* this cross-references a separate March 2023 proposal amending the Cross-Border Enforcement Directive, which the Section 8 enforcement discussion below relies on.

FACT: "Regulation, adopted by the Commission on 14 February 2023 24 , extends the scope to almost all newly registered HD" *Source: COM(2023) 445 final.* https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:52023PC0445 *Analytical inference:* this is the CO2 Standards Regulation (2019/1242) revision, a separate but complementary EU HDV instrument; its own 2030 CO2-target milestone is a distinct forward event from this directive's own trilogue timeline.

FACT: "A dedicated EU web portal should be set up to provide information about the roads where EMS are allowed to circulate (as well as the national maximum authorised weights and dimensions of vehicles in Member States)." *Source: European Parliament Legislative Train Schedule, as of the export date.* https://www.europarl.europa.eu/legislative-train/theme-a-european-green-deal/file-revision-of-the-weights-and-dimensions-directive *Operational implication:* this would be a post-enactment deliverable, not available before the directive is adopted.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this brief's own corpus includes only a truncated capture of COM(2023) 445 final's own explanatory memorandum (roughly 30,000 characters of a longer document); a workspace with a specific compliance question should confirm current status directly against the full EUR-Lex record rather than relying solely on this summary.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: What is a "zero-emission vehicle" for the purpose of the weight bonus?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* FACT: "ZEVs may receive a weight bonus to account for heavier technology, with different allowances for 5-axle and 6-axle vehicles to protect infrastructure." *Source: European Parliament Legislative Train Schedule, as of the export date.* https://www.europarl.europa.eu/legislative-train/theme-a-european-green-deal/file-revision-of-the-weights-and-dimensions-directive The precise legal definition of "zero-emission vehicle" for this directive -- whether plug-in hybrids or hydrogen fuel-cell vehicles qualify -- must be confirmed from the final enacted text; this corpus does not reproduce a definitions article.

**Q2: Does the 44-tonne cross-border facilitation have a sunset clause?**

*Analytical inference:* Yes, under the Parliament's own position. FACT: "would allow 44-tonne fossil-fuel (diesel) trucks to circulate in cross-border traffic until 31 December 2034" *Source: Platform for Electromobility, 15 January 2026.* https://www.platformelectromobility.eu/2026/01/15/weight-dimensions-directive-prioritising-decarbonisation/ *Legal Confirmation Required:* the Council's own position on this sunset clause, and whether it survives trilogue, requires confirmation once a final text exists.

**Q3: Do EMS cross-border permissions require a bilateral agreement?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* FACT: "clarifying that Member States who allow European Modular Systems (EMS) in their territories, will also be able to use them in international operations among neighboring Member States which allow EMS, without a need for a bilateral agreement and without a restriction of crossing only one border." *Source: European Parliament Legislative Train Schedule, as of the export date.* https://www.europarl.europa.eu/legislative-train/theme-a-european-green-deal/file-revision-of-the-weights-and-dimensions-directive Whether the final directive removes the bilateral-agreement requirement is subject to trilogue resolution.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: All provisions described below are from the Commission proposal (COM(2023) 445 final) and the legislative positions of Parliament and Council, not from enacted law. Binding verbs describe what the proposal/positions provide, not enacted obligations.*

## A. Zero-emission vehicle weight bonus

FACT: "a necessary allowance for weights or dimensions to compensate for the weight and/or size of the relevant technology and ensure at least the same loading capacity as conventional HDVs that run on fossil fuels." *Source: COM(2023) 445 final.* https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:52023PC0445

FACT: "The Parliament report proposes to increase the maximum weight of zero-emission trucks by four tonnes, to compensate the space and weight needed to fit battery or hydrogen cells, and to provide additional loading capacity." *Source: European Parliament Legislative Train Schedule, as of the export date.* https://www.europarl.europa.eu/legislative-train/theme-a-european-green-deal/file-revision-of-the-weights-and-dimensions-directive

FACT: "The supports the transition to zero-emission vehicles (ZEVs) while limiting potential road damage. ZEVs may receive a weight bonus to account for heavier technology, with different allowances for 5-axle and 6-axle vehicles to protect infrastructure." *Source: European Parliament Legislative Train Schedule, as of the export date.* https://www.europarl.europa.eu/legislative-train/theme-a-european-green-deal/file-revision-of-the-weights-and-dimensions-directive (the captured source text itself omits a word before "supports"; based on the surrounding sentences this describes the Council's general approach, reproduced exactly as captured rather than silently corrected)

FACT: "endorses the proposal to allow a maximum additional weight of 4 tonnes for zero-emission (ZE) lorries only, but calls for a rigorous monitoring policy post-adoption, including immediate policy change should the desired impact not be achieved" *Source: EESC Press Summary, 6 October 2023.* https://www.eesc.europa.eu/en/news-media/press-summaries/revision-weights-and-dimensions-directive-9653ec

FACT: "Weight exemptions for zero-emission vehicles" *Source: IRU, 12 March 2024.* https://www.iru.org/news-resources/newsroom/parliament-backs-immediate-smart-greening-eu-road-transport *Analytical inference:* the IRU's own framing of the weight bonus as a "weight exemption" is the clearest unnegated exemption language this corpus offers for the ZEV weight bonus mechanism.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the weight bonus applies to a zero-emission tractor paired with a conventional trailer, or only to a full zero-emission combination, requires confirmation from the final directive text; the Platform for Electromobility states that the bonus is not available for a diesel tractor paired with a zero-emission trailer.

## B. Length (dimension) derogation for zero-emission vehicles

FACT: "They may also be up to 0.9 m longer to make room for zero-emission equipment." *Source: European Parliament Legislative Train Schedule, as of the export date.* https://www.europarl.europa.eu/legislative-train/theme-a-european-green-deal/file-revision-of-the-weights-and-dimensions-directive

FACT: "provided this does not compromise interoperability with intermodal terminal or rail operations, and as long as the turning circle requirement is met" *Source: Platform for Electromobility, 15 January 2026.* https://www.platformelectromobility.eu/2026/01/15/weight-dimensions-directive-prioritising-decarbonisation/ *Analytical inference:* this is the interoperability condition the Parliament attaches to its own broader length-derogation proposal, which the Council's 0.9 m cap does not carry in the same form; trilogue will determine the final provision.

## C. Cross-border facilitation -- 44-tonne standard combinations

FACT: "zero-emission vehicles or vehicle combinations involved in intermodal transport may cross borders even if they exceed directive weight limits, as long as they remain within the limits permitted in both countries." *Source: European Parliament Legislative Train Schedule, as of the export date.* https://www.europarl.europa.eu/legislative-train/theme-a-european-green-deal/file-revision-of-the-weights-and-dimensions-directive

FACT: "would allow 44-tonne fossil-fuel (diesel) trucks to circulate in cross-border traffic until 31 December 2034" *Source: Platform for Electromobility, 15 January 2026.* https://www.platformelectromobility.eu/2026/01/15/weight-dimensions-directive-prioritising-decarbonisation/

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the Council general approach's own position on this sunset date is not fully stated in this corpus; confirmation requires the Council's own press release or the final trilogue text.

## D. Intermodal transport extra weight and height allowances

FACT: "lorries, trailers and semitrailers carrying out these operations will be allowed to carry some extra weight. Extra height allowances will also facilitate the transport of high-cube containers by standard vehicles." *Source: European Parliament Legislative Train Schedule, as of the export date.* https://www.europarl.europa.eu/legislative-train/theme-a-european-green-deal/file-revision-of-the-weights-and-dimensions-directive *Specific numerical values for the intermodal extra weight and height allowances are not stated in this corpus.*

## E. Aerodynamic devices and energy-saving equipment

FACT: "The uptake of more aerodynamic cabins and other energy-saving devices will also be encouraged, improving driver comfort, safety, and the energy efficiency of vehicles." *Source: European Parliament Legislative Train Schedule, as of the export date.* https://www.europarl.europa.eu/legislative-train/theme-a-european-green-deal/file-revision-of-the-weights-and-dimensions-directive

FACT: "The use of alternative ly fuel led HDV s and improved aerodynamics to increase the energy efficiency of road transport operations and reduce GHG emissions has not yet yielded meaningful results" *Source: COM(2023) 445 final.* https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:52023PC0445 *Analytical inference:* the Commission's own ex-post evaluation found limited real-world effect from the current directive's aerodynamic-device incentives, which is the evidentiary basis for strengthening them in this proposal.

## F. European Modular Systems (EMS)

FACT: "clarifying that Member States who allow European Modular Systems (EMS) in their territories, will also be able to use them in international operations among neighboring Member States which allow EMS, without a need for a bilateral agreement and without a restriction of crossing only one border." *Source: European Parliament Legislative Train Schedule, as of the export date.* https://www.europarl.europa.eu/legislative-train/theme-a-european-green-deal/file-revision-of-the-weights-and-dimensions-directive

FACT: "It also strengthens the governance framework applying to European modular systems (EMS), with an prior assessment for the impacts on road safety, road infrastructure, modal cooperation and the environment." *Source: European Parliament Legislative Train Schedule, as of the export date.* https://www.europarl.europa.eu/legislative-train/theme-a-european-green-deal/file-revision-of-the-weights-and-dimensions-directive *Analytical inference:* this adds a prior-impact-assessment gate to EMS deployment not present in the Commission's original proposal.

## G. Enforcement reform

FACT: "would oblige Member States to install certified automatic systems that recognize vehicles which exceed maximum weight limits and propose that Member States implement intelligent access policies to regulate and monitor the access of heavy duty vehicles to specific roads." *Source: European Parliament Legislative Train Schedule, as of the export date.* https://www.europarl.europa.eu/legislative-train/theme-a-european-green-deal/file-revision-of-the-weights-and-dimensions-directive

FACT: "extending its scope to other road-safety-related traffic offences" *Source: COM(2023) 445 final.* https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:52023PC0445 *Operational implication:* this cross-references a separate March 2023 Commission proposal amending the Cross-Border Enforcement Directive, which would make overloading offences easier to prosecute across a Member State border.

## H. Penalty provision

*Specific penalty provision not available from primary sources as of the export date.* The proposal references enforcement reform (item G above) but leaves specific fines and sanctions to Member State transposition. *Legal Confirmation Required:* penalty exposure for overloading under any future national transposition, and any cross-border penalty-recognition mechanism, requires legal review per Member State of operation.

No exceptions are stated in Sections A through H above.

Obligations surveyed: 8; workspace-adjacent: 8; extracted as FACT: 16.

# 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*No content for this section as of the export date: this directive regulates vehicle categories (HDVs, including their zero-emission variants) operated by carriers, not a product or service category a freight forwarder itself offers; no source in this corpus states a product-specific compliance status running to a freight-forwarding service as such.*

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

As proposed, the directive does not impose direct registration or reporting obligations on freight forwarders as a defined category; primary registration and reporting obligations fall on Member States (to report enforcement data) and vehicle operators (to comply with weight documentation requirements).

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether national transposition measures will impose documentation or reporting requirements on freight forwarders or load organisers requires legal review per Member State.

FACT: "A dedicated EU web portal should be set up to provide information about the roads where EMS are allowed to circulate (as well as the national maximum authorised weights and dimensions of vehicles in Member States)." *Source: European Parliament Legislative Train Schedule, as of the export date.* https://www.europarl.europa.eu/legislative-train/theme-a-european-green-deal/file-revision-of-the-weights-and-dimensions-directive *Operational implication:* once established (post-enactment), this would be a primary operational reference for cross-border HDV route planning.

*Specific registration or reporting format not available from primary sources as of the export date.*

# 11. Operational System Requirements

*Note: because no source in this corpus states an operational-system requirement running to a freight forwarder today, this section records monitoring and readiness infrastructure a workspace should maintain rather than a system the proposal itself requires.*

*Operational implication:* A workspace should establish a carrier-profile data field capturing ZEV fleet share and weight-bonus eligibility, so procurement decisions can leverage the weight bonus once enacted.

FACT: "would oblige Member States to install certified automatic systems that recognize vehicles which exceed maximum weight limits and propose that Member States implement intelligent access policies to regulate and monitor the access of heavy duty vehicles to specific roads." *Source: European Parliament Legislative Train Schedule, as of the export date.* https://www.europarl.europa.eu/legislative-train/theme-a-european-green-deal/file-revision-of-the-weights-and-dimensions-directive *Operational implication:* the mandatory weigh-in-motion system requirement in the Parliament position would systematically increase detection of overloaded vehicles; workspaces relying on shipper-provided cargo weight declarations without verification should review those procedures ahead of this potential enforcement intensification.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

FACT: "The Council maintains existing flexibilities to exceed standard weights and dimensions for vehicles with special permits carrying indivisible loads, for operations that have little impact on international competition, and for European Modular Systems." *Source: European Parliament Legislative Train Schedule, as of the export date.* https://www.europarl.europa.eu/legislative-train/theme-a-european-green-deal/file-revision-of-the-weights-and-dimensions-directive *Operational implication:* for workspaces moving indivisible loads that currently require special permits, this exemption is expected to be preserved under the revised directive.

FACT: "It would also allow additional length for shuttle services to improve efficiency." *Source: European Parliament Legislative Train Schedule, as of the export date.* https://www.europarl.europa.eu/legislative-train/theme-a-european-green-deal/file-revision-of-the-weights-and-dimensions-directive *Specific definition of "shuttle services" eligible for this length derogation is not stated in this corpus.*

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

FACT: "The EU truck fleet (above 3.5 tonnes) continues to be largely dominated by fossil fuel engines, with 96.3% of all trucks in the EU run ning on diesel, and only 0.7% of all trucks run ning on alternatively fuelled internal combustion engines (natural gas and LPG). The share of electrically chargeable trucks, including electric and plug - in hybrid vehicles, is as low as 0.2%." *Source: COM(2023) 445 final.* https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:52023PC0445

FACT: "on of zero-emission trucks grew from 0.6% in 2016 to 7% in 2020. It is go ing in the right direction, but not fast" *Source: COM(2023) 445 final.* https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:52023PC0445 (mid-sentence fragment, reproduced exactly as captured)

*Analytical inference:* The very low ZEV share in the HDV fleet as of this evaluation means the weight bonus, even if enacted promptly, will have limited near-term effect on the majority of carrier fleets; workspaces should not assume rapid carrier conversion to ZEV-eligible fleets.

FACT: "The European Research and Innovation framework programmes have been supporting low and zero-emission HDVs, aerodynamic features and energy efficiency challenges with specific partnerships since 2007 with the European Green Cars Initiative under FP7, the European Green Vehicle Initiative under Horizon 2020 and currently with the Towards Zero Emission Road Transport under Horizon Europe." *Source: COM(2023) 445 final.* https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:52023PC0445

FACT: "Specific projects delivered some of the innovations, such as powered zero emission trailers and improved aerodynamics" *Source: COM(2023) 445 final.* https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:52023PC0445 *Analytical inference:* workspaces tracking the carrier equipment market should monitor the deployment timeline for powered zero-emission trailers, which may interact with the weight-bonus qualification question (ZEV tractor vs. ZEV trailer vs. full ZEV combination).
